# Google GenerativeAI .NET SDK — Documentation

The unofficial .NET SDK for **Google Gemini** (Gemini API / Google AI Studio) and **Vertex AI**. It is a REST-based,
NativeAOT-compatible client covering content generation, multimodal input, structured output, function calling,
the Live API, the Interactions API, File Search, batch processing, tuning, RAG and more.

> **Version 4.0** brings parity with the latest Google APIs. Upgrading from 3.x? Start with the
> [Migration Guide](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Migration-Guide-v4) and the [Release Notes](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Release-Notes-v4).

## Packages

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`Google_GenerativeAI`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI) | Core SDK: models, clients and types for the Gemini API and Vertex AI. |
| [`Google_GenerativeAI.Tools`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI.Tools) | Function calling helpers, source-generated tools and MCP integration. |
| [`Google_GenerativeAI.Auth`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI.Auth) | OAuth, service account and Application Default Credentials authenticators. |
| [`Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft) | `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` implementations (`IChatClient`, embeddings, images). |
| [`Google_GenerativeAI.Web`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI.Web) | Dependency injection and configuration for ASP.NET Core. |
| [`Google_GenerativeAI.Live`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI.Live) | Real-time Multimodal Live API and Live Music over WebSockets. |

Supported frameworks: .NET 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11, .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Framework 4.6.2.

## Start here

1. [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization) — create a `GoogleAi` or `VertexAI` client and a model.
2. [Authentication](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication) — API keys, ADC, service accounts and OAuth.
3. [Generate Content](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Generate-Content) — your first request, then [Streaming](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Streaming) and [Chat Session](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Chat-Session).
4. [Supported Models](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Supported-Models) — current model constants and their replacements for retired models.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization -->

This page shows how to set up the SDK for the **Gemini Developer API** (`GoogleAi`) and for **Vertex AI** (`VertexAI`). You can configure it from environment variables, constructors or platform adapters.

```bash
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI
```

Most types live in the `GenerativeAI` and `GenerativeAI.Types` namespaces. For credentials (API keys, ADC, OAuth, service accounts), see [Authentication](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication).

## Environment Variables

If you set these variables, you can leave the matching constructor arguments out:

| Variable | Used for |
|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | API key for the Gemini API (and for Vertex AI express mode). Read when you don't pass an `apiKey`. |
| `GOOGLE_AI_MODEL` | Default model name, used when a model is created with a `null` model name. Defaults to `GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel` (`models/gemini-3.8-flash`). |
| `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` | Google Cloud project for Vertex AI. If it isn't set, the SDK reads `project_id` from the credentials file. |
| `GOOGLE_REGION` | Vertex AI location. Defaults to `us-central1` when not set. |
| `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | A ready-made OAuth access token for Vertex AI. |
| `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | Path to a credentials file (ADC / service account) for Vertex AI. |
| `GOOGLE_WEB_CREDENTIALS` | Path to OAuth web credentials. This file is checked before `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`. |
| `GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION` | API version to use when none is passed to a platform adapter. This is the same variable the official SDKs read. `beta` maps to `v1beta` on the Gemini API and `v1beta1` on Vertex AI. Any other value, such as `v1`, is used as-is. |

> **Note:** The SDK reads `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. It does not read `GEMINI_API_KEY`. If your environment uses `GEMINI_API_KEY`, pass its value explicitly: `new GoogleAi(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GEMINI_API_KEY"))`.

> **Tip:** `GenerativeAI.Types` contains a type named `Environment`. In files that have `using GenerativeAI.Types;`, write `System.Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(...)` to avoid a CS0104 ambiguity error.

> **Note on `GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION`:** The Gemini API defaults to `v1beta` and Vertex AI to `v1beta1`. The variable applies to `GoogleAi`, `GoogleAIPlatformAdapter` and `VertextPlatformAdapter` when you don't pass `apiVersion`. The `VertexAI(...)` convenience constructor always passes its `apiVersion` argument (default `ApiVersions.v1Beta1`), so on Vertex the variable only takes effect when you create the `VertextPlatformAdapter` yourself.

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;

// GOOGLE_API_KEY is set in the environment
var ai = new GoogleAi();
var model = ai.CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);

var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Hello!");
Console.WriteLine(response.Text());
```

## Gemini Developer API (`GoogleAi`)

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;

// API key from the constructor (or from GOOGLE_API_KEY when omitted)
var ai = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY");

// Generic model
GenerativeModel model = ai.CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);

// GeminiModel adds file helpers (upload by file path, the Files client)
GeminiModel gemini = ai.CreateGeminiModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
```

`CreateGenerativeModel` and `CreateGeminiModel` also take an optional `GenerationConfig`, safety settings and a system instruction:

```csharp
var model = ai.CreateGenerativeModel(
    GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash,
    config: new GenerationConfig { Temperature = 0.7, MaxOutputTokens = 1024 },
    systemInstruction: "You are a concise assistant.");
```

The `GoogleAi` constructor signature is `GoogleAi(string? apiKey = null, string? accessToken = null, HttpClient? client = null, ILogger? logger = null)`. Pass `accessToken` (or an authenticator through the adapter) for endpoints that need OAuth, such as tuning and semantic retrieval.

## Vertex AI (`VertexAI`)

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;

var vertex = new VertexAI(projectId: "your-project-id", region: "global");
var model = vertex.CreateGenerativeModel(VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Flash);
```

Full constructor:

```csharp
public VertexAI(string? projectId = null, string? region = null, string? accessToken = null,
    bool expressMode = false, string? apiKey = null, string apiVersion = ApiVersions.v1Beta1,
    HttpClient? httpClient = null, IGoogleAuthenticator? authenticator = null, ILogger? logger = null)
```

If you leave out `projectId` and `region`, the SDK uses `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` and `GOOGLE_REGION`. If no project ID is found there, it reads `project_id` from the credentials file.

### Choosing a region: `global` vs. regional

- **`global`**: The newest Gemini models (for example the Gemini 3.x family) are served only from the `global` location. With `region: "global"` the SDK calls `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/...` instead of `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/...`.
- **Regional (for example `us-central1`)**: Use a regional location for the [Vertex RAG Engine](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Vertex-RAG-Engine) and for embedding models that are not served globally, such as `gemini-embedding-001` and `text-embedding-005` (see [Embeddings](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Embeddings)).

You can create two `VertexAI` instances, one for each location:

```csharp
var global   = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "global");      // chat / generation
var regional = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "us-central1"); // RAG, embeddings
```

### Express mode (API key)

Vertex AI express mode uses an API key instead of a Google Cloud project:

```csharp
var vertex = new VertexAI(expressMode: true, apiKey: "YOUR_VERTEX_API_KEY");
var model = vertex.CreateGenerativeModel(VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Flash);
```

Express mode throws `ArgumentException` when no API key is passed and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is not set.

## Platform Adapters

`GoogleAi` and `VertexAI` are wrappers around an `IPlatformAdapter` (namespace `GenerativeAI.Core`). Create the adapter yourself when you need to control the API version, authenticator or token validation, or when you want to share one adapter between models and clients (`FileClient`, `CachingClient`, `ModelClient`, `EmbeddingModel`, ...).

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Core;

// Gemini API
IPlatformAdapter googleAdapter = new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter("YOUR_API_KEY", apiVersion: ApiVersions.v1Beta);
var ai = new GoogleAi(googleAdapter);
var model = ai.CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);

// Vertex AI (note the class name: VertextPlatformAdapter)
IPlatformAdapter vertexAdapter = new VertextPlatformAdapter(projectId: "your-project-id", region: "global");
var vertex = new VertexAI(vertexAdapter);
var vertexModel = vertex.CreateGenerativeModel(VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Flash);

// Adapters can also be passed to models and clients directly
var direct = new GenerativeModel(googleAdapter, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
```

Available API versions are on `ApiVersions`: `v1`, `v1Beta`, `v1Beta1` and `v1Alpha`.

## Custom HttpClient and Logging

Every entry point takes an optional `HttpClient` and `ILogger`:

```csharp
var http = new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5) };
var ai = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY", client: http, logger: myLogger);
```

## Choosing an Initialization Method

| Method | Best for |
|---|---|
| Environment variables | Quick setup, development, containers and CI |
| `GoogleAi` / `VertexAI` constructors | Most applications |
| Platform adapters | Custom API versions or auth, or sharing one adapter between many clients |

## Error Handling

When an API call fails, the SDK throws `GenerativeAI.Exceptions.ApiException` with `ErrorCode` (HTTP or API code), `ErrorStatus` (for example `INVALID_ARGUMENT` or `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`) and `ErrorMessage`. See [Generate Content](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Generate-Content#error-handling).

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication -->

This page covers the ways the SDK can authenticate with the Gemini Developer API (`GoogleAi`) and Vertex AI (`VertexAI`). For constructors and environment variables, see [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization).

## Overview

| Platform | Method | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini API | API key (constructor or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`) | `Google_GenerativeAI` |
| Gemini API | OAuth access token / authenticator (tuning, semantic retrieval) | `Google_GenerativeAI` (+ `Google_GenerativeAI.Auth` for authenticators) |
| Vertex AI | Application Default Credentials (`GoogleCloudAdcAuthenticator`) | `Google_GenerativeAI` |
| Vertex AI | Access token (constructor or `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN`) | `Google_GenerativeAI` |
| Vertex AI | OAuth user flow (`GoogleOAuthAuthenticator`) | `Google_GenerativeAI.Auth` |
| Vertex AI | Service account (`GoogleServiceAccountAuthenticator`) | `Google_GenerativeAI.Auth` |
| Vertex AI | Express mode with an API key | `Google_GenerativeAI` |

Authenticators implement `IGoogleAuthenticator` (namespace `GenerativeAI.Core`). The concrete classes are in the `GenerativeAI.Authenticators` namespace. Pass one through the `authenticator` parameter of `VertexAI`, `VertexAIModel`, `GoogleAIPlatformAdapter` or `VertextPlatformAdapter`. The SDK then gets, validates and refreshes access tokens for you.

```bash
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Auth   # only for OAuth / service-account authenticators
```

## Gemini API

### API key

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;

// From the environment
Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("GOOGLE_API_KEY", "YOUR_API_KEY");
var ai = new GoogleAi();

// Or explicitly
var ai2 = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY");
```

If neither is available, `GoogleAIPlatformAdapter` throws `ArgumentException("API Key is required for Google Gemini AI.")`.

### OAuth access token (tuned models, semantic retrieval)

Some Gemini API endpoints need an OAuth access token in addition to the API key:

```csharp
// A token you already have
var ai = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY", accessToken: "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN");

// Or an authenticator that gets and refreshes tokens
using GenerativeAI.Authenticators;

var adapter = new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter("YOUR_API_KEY",
    authenticator: new GoogleServiceAccountAuthenticator("path/to/service_account.json"));
var ai3 = new GoogleAi(adapter);
```

`GoogleAi.CreateCorpusManager(authenticator)` and `GoogleAi.CreatSemanticRetrieverModel(modelName, authenticator: ...)` require an authenticator. See [Semantic Search Retrieval with Google AQA](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Legacy-Semantic-Retrieval-(AQA)).

## Vertex AI

When you pass neither an authenticator nor an access token, Vertex AI uses **Application Default Credentials**. It looks for credentials in `GOOGLE_WEB_CREDENTIALS`, then `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, then the gcloud default file (`%APPDATA%/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`, or the equivalent path on Linux and macOS).

### Application Default Credentials (ADC)

`GoogleCloudAdcAuthenticator` is part of the core package. It gets tokens by running `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`, so the gcloud CLI must be installed and you must have run `gcloud auth application-default login`.

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Authenticators;

var vertex = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "global",
    authenticator: new GoogleCloudAdcAuthenticator());

// Equivalent, using the platform adapter
var adapter = new VertextPlatformAdapter("your-project-id", "global",
    new GoogleCloudAdcAuthenticator());
var vertex2 = new VertexAI(adapter);
```

### Access token

```csharp
var vertex = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "global", accessToken: "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN");
// or set GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN
```

### Service account (`Google_GenerativeAI.Auth`)

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Authenticators;

// JSON key file (recommended)
var authenticator = new GoogleServiceAccountAuthenticator("path/to/service_account.json");

// Or a stream with the JSON key
// var authenticator = new GoogleServiceAccountAuthenticator(File.OpenRead("service_account.json"));

// Or service-account email + .p12 certificate (+ passphrase)
// var authenticator = new GoogleServiceAccountAuthenticator("sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com", "key.p12", "notasecret");

var vertex = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "global", authenticator: authenticator);

// Or via the adapter
var adapter = new VertextPlatformAdapter("your-project-id", "global", authenticator);
var vertex2 = new VertexAI(platformAdapter: adapter);
```

### OAuth user flow (`Google_GenerativeAI.Auth`)

`GoogleOAuthAuthenticator` takes the path to an OAuth **client secret** JSON file (default `client_secret.json`). It runs the browser-based consent flow and stores the token in `token.json`.

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Authenticators;

var authenticator = new GoogleOAuthAuthenticator("path/to/client_secret.json");
var vertex = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "global", authenticator: authenticator);
```

### Express mode (API key)

```csharp
var vertex = new VertexAI(expressMode: true, apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY");
```

Express mode needs no project ID or OAuth token. It throws `ArgumentException` if no API key is passed and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is not set.

### Getting a token directly

```csharp
var token = await authenticator.GetAccessTokenAsync();
Console.WriteLine(token?.AccessToken);
```

# Configuration and Error Handling

This page covers the environment variables the SDK reads, Vertex AI locations, `HttpClient` and `ILogger` injection,
timeouts, and the exceptions the SDK throws.

---

## Environment variables

The SDK reads these variables through the `GenerativeAI.EnvironmentVariables` class. A value you pass in code always
wins over the environment variable.

| Variable | Used for | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Gemini API key. `GoogleAIPlatformAdapter` uses it when you pass `null`. `VertextPlatformAdapter` uses it as the Vertex AI Express key. `LiveMusicClient(apiKey: null)` also uses it | none |
| `GOOGLE_AI_MODEL` | Model used when none is passed (`GenerativeModel`, `VertexAIModel`, `AddGenerativeAI()`) | `GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel` (`models/gemini-3.8-flash`) |
| `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` | Vertex AI project ID. With `AddGenerativeAI()`, setting it also switches the default to Vertex AI | read from the credentials file |
| `GOOGLE_REGION` | Vertex AI location | `us-central1` |
| `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` | OAuth access token for Vertex AI | none |
| `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | Path to a service account or ADC JSON file (Vertex AI) | `%APPDATA%/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json` |
| `GOOGLE_WEB_CREDENTIALS` | Path to OAuth web credentials. Vertex AI checks it **before** `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | none |
| `GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION` | **New in v4.** The default API version when none is passed. `beta` means `v1beta` on the Gemini API and `v1beta1` on Vertex AI. Any other value, such as `v1`, is used as written | `v1beta` (Gemini API) / `v1beta1` (Vertex AI) |

Notes:

- The SDK reads `GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION` every time it creates a platform adapter. It reads the other variables once,
  when the app starts (they are `static readonly` fields).
- `GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION` only applies when the API version is left as `null`. The `GoogleAIPlatformAdapter` and
  `VertextPlatformAdapter` constructors now take `string? apiVersion = null`, and so do `GoogleAi`,
  `GenerativeModel(apiKey, ...)` and `VertexAIModel`. The `VertexAI(...)` convenience constructor still defaults
  `apiVersion` to `ApiVersions.v1Beta1`, so it ignores the variable unless you pass `apiVersion: null`.
- The defaults stay on the beta versions because previews, the Live API and TTS are only on `v1beta`.
- `ApiVersions` has `v1`, `v1Beta`, `v1Beta1`, and the new `v1Alpha`. Ephemeral Live API auth tokens use `v1Alpha`.

```csharp
// Pin the API version in code
var adapter = new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey, apiVersion: ApiVersions.v1);

// Or for the whole process
Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION", "v1");
var model = new GenerativeModel(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash); // uses v1
```

### ASP.NET Core (`Google_GenerativeAI.Web`)

`AddGenerativeAI()` fills any option you didn't set from the variables above. Here is how it decides between the
Gemini API and Vertex AI:

- `AddGenerativeAI()` and `AddGenerativeAI(IConfiguration)`: if `IsVertex` isn't set, the app uses Vertex AI when
  `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` is set.
- `AddGenerativeAI(GenerativeAIOptions)`: **changed in v4.** If you pass an API key (`Credentials.ApiKey`) but no
  `ProjectId`, leave `IsVertex` unset and don't enable `ExpressMode`, the app now uses the **Gemini API**, even when
  `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` is set. Set `IsVertex` to choose explicitly.

See [Web Application Integration](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Web-Application-Integration).

---

## Vertex AI locations

The location (region) decides which endpoint the SDK calls:

| Region | Base URL |
|---|---|
| `global` | `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/{version}/projects/{project}/locations/global/...` |
| any other, for example `us-central1` | `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/{version}/projects/{project}/locations/{region}/...` |
| Express mode | `BaseUrls.VertexAIExpress` (API key, no project or location) |

Google serves the newest Gemini models (Gemini 4, 3.x) on Vertex AI from the `global` location. Some services are only
available in regional locations, such as the RAG Engine and some tuning or batch features. For those, use a regional
location such as `us-central1`.

```csharp
var vertex = new VertexAI(projectId: "my-project", region: "global");
// or: set GOOGLE_REGION=global
```

---

## HttpClient, logging and timeouts

Every client and model accepts an optional `HttpClient` and an optional `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger`:

```csharp
using var http = new HttpClient { Timeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) };
ILogger logger = loggerFactory.CreateLogger("Gemini");

var model = new GenerativeModel(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash, httpClient: http, logger: logger);

var googleAi = new GoogleAi(apiKey, client: http, logger: logger); // models/clients it creates share http + logger
var files = new FileClient(new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey, logger: logger), http, logger);
```

- If you don't pass an `HttpClient`, each client creates its own, with a **5-minute timeout** and
  `User-Agent: Google_GenerativeAI SDK`. In long-running apps, pass a shared or `IHttpClientFactory`-managed client.
- The logger receives non-success status codes (URLs have the API key masked) and, for some clients, request
  diagnostics. Platform adapters also take a `logger` parameter.
- Cancellation: every async method takes a `CancellationToken`. In v4, embedding calls pass it all the way to the
  HTTP request. Before v4, `EmbedContentAsync`/`BatchEmbedContentAsync` ignored it.
- Long-running operations: `VertexRagManager.LongRunningOperationTimeout` defaults to 5 minutes, and
  `AwaitForLongRunningOperation(operationId, timeOut, ...)` now honours the `timeOut` (milliseconds) you pass.
  Several clients, such as Interactions, File Search, Tuning and Triggers, have `WaitFor...Async` helpers with their
  own poll interval and timeout parameters.
- **Retries:** the SDK doesn't retry failed HTTP requests on its own. To retry on 429 or 5xx, add a policy to the
  `HttpClient` you pass, for example `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` or Polly. Some features have their own
  recovery logic, listed below.

### Automatic recovery features (v4)

| Feature | Setting | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `generateContent` continuation tokens: when Google ends a response early (`FinishReason.CONTINUATION`), the SDK re-sends the request with the token and merges the results. Streams continue the same way, including after a dropped stream that had reached a checkpoint | `GenerativeModel.EnableAutomaticContinuation`, `GenerativeModel.MaxContinuations` | `true`, 10 |
| Interactions continuation (`requires_continuation`) | `InteractionsClient.EnableAutomaticContinuation`, `MaxContinuations` | `true`, 10 |
| Resuming a dropped Interactions stream from the last event | `InteractionsClient.MaxStreamReconnects` | 3 |
| Live API: re-send setup (and resume the session) after the WebSocket reconnects | `MultiModalLiveClient.ResendSetupOnReconnect` | `true` |

```csharp
var model = new GenerativeModel(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash)
{
    EnableAutomaticContinuation = false // receive the partial response and token yourself
};
```

---

## Exceptions

All exception types are in the `GenerativeAI.Exceptions` namespace.

| Exception | When it's thrown | Useful members |
|---|---|---|
| `ApiException` | Google returned an error response that the SDK could parse (any non-2xx with a Google error body) | `ErrorCode` (int, usually the HTTP or RPC code), `ErrorStatus` (for example `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`), `ErrorMessage`; `Message` is `"{status} (Code: {code}): {message}"` |
| `HttpRequestException` | A non-2xx response with a body that isn't a Google error (for example HTML from a proxy). In v4 the message includes the status code and up to 500 characters of the body | `Message` |
| `VertexAIException` | A Vertex AI long-running operation, for example a RAG Engine import or corpus operation, finished with an error | `Status` (`GoogleRpcStatus` with `Code`, `Message`, `Details`) |
| `GenerativeAIException` | SDK-side failures: a response blocked by safety filters (the block reason is in `Details`), a call to a function the model doesn't know (unless `FunctionCallingBehaviour.AutoHandleBadFunctionCalls` is on), a failed file or File Search operation, or a missing authenticator for the corpus manager | `Message`, `Details` |
| `FileTooLargeException` | A file is bigger than the upload limit | `Message` |
| `NotSupportedException` | You called a feature the current platform doesn't support. Examples: Veo on the Gemini API, `WebhookConfig` on Vertex AI batch jobs, Vertex-only embedding options on the Gemini API, an unsupported embedding model | `Message` explains the alternative |
| `ArgumentException` / `ArgumentNullException` | Missing required arguments, for example no API key for the Gemini API | |

### How the SDK parses error responses (v4)

When a request fails, `ApiBase` reads the response body and tries to turn it into an `ApiException`:

1. It accepts both `{"error": {...}}` and the array form `[{"error": {...}}]`. Some endpoints return the array form,
   for example 402 prepayment errors.
2. It needs `error.message`. It takes `error.code` when the code is numeric and **otherwise uses the HTTP status code**.
   It uses `error.status` when present, or `"Unknown status"`.
3. If the body is empty, isn't JSON, or has no `error.message`, the SDK throws `HttpRequestException` with the status
   code and a truncated body.

In v4 the same handling applies to **all** requests, including **streaming** (`StreamContentAsync`) and **file
uploads**. In v3.x those threw a bare `HttpRequestException` (from `EnsureSuccessStatusCode`) with no Google details.

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Exceptions;

try
{
    var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Hello");
    Console.WriteLine(response.Text());
}
catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.ErrorCode == 429 || ex.ErrorStatus == "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED")
{
    // quota or rate limit: back off and retry
}
catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.ErrorStatus == "INVALID_ARGUMENT")
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Bad request: {ex.ErrorMessage}");
}
catch (ApiException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{ex.ErrorStatus} ({ex.ErrorCode}): {ex.ErrorMessage}");
}
catch (HttpRequestException ex)
{
    // non-Google error body (proxy, network appliance, etc.)
    Console.WriteLine(ex.Message);
}
```

### Live API errors

`MultiModalLiveClient` reports errors through the `ErrorOccurred` event instead of throwing on the WebSocket thread.
In v4, exceptions thrown inside your own event handlers are caught and reported there as well, so they no longer
crash the process. A `GoAwayReceived` event means the server will close the connection soon. Its
`LiveServerGoAway.TimeLeft` / `TimeLeftDuration` tells you how long you have. See [Multimodal Live API](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Live-API).


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Supported-Models -->

# Supported Models

The SDK ships model ID constants in two static classes in the `GenerativeAI` namespace:

- `GoogleAIModels`: Gemini API (Google AI Studio) model IDs, most with the `models/` prefix.
- `VertexAIModels`: Vertex AI model IDs, without a prefix.

You can always pass any model ID string yourself. The constants are a convenience and follow Google's
[models](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models) and [deprecations](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations)
pages as of the v4.0.0 release.

```csharp
var model = new GenerativeModel(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
```

`GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel` is `Gemini38Flash` (`models/gemini-3.8-flash`). It was `gemini-2.5-flash` in v3.x.
The SDK uses it when you don't pass a model and the `GOOGLE_AI_MODEL` environment variable is not set.

> **Vertex AI and the `global` location:** Google serves the newest Gemini models on Vertex AI from the `global`
> location. With `region: "global"`, the SDK uses the `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com` endpoint instead of
> `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com`. If a new model returns "not found" in a regional location, try `global`:
>
> ```csharp
> var vertex = new VertexAI(projectId: "my-project", region: "global");
> var model = vertex.CreateGenerativeModel(VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Flash);
> ```

---

`Gemini25ProPreview0325`, `Gemini25FlashPreviewTTS`, `Gemini3ProPreview` and `Gemini3ProImagePreview`. They are not
marked `[Obsolete]` in this class, but many of them are retired on Vertex AI as well. Use the current IDs above.

### `VertexAIModels.Embeddings`

| Constant | Model ID |
|---|---|
| `GeminiEmbedding001` | `gemini-embedding-001` |
| `TextMultilingualEmbedding002` | `text-multilingual-embedding-002` |
| `TextEmbedding004` | `text-embedding-004` |
| `TextEmbeddingGecko001` / `002` / `003` | `textembedding-gecko@001` / `@002` / `@003` |
| `TextEmbeddingGeckoMultilingual001` | `textembedding-gecko-multilingual@001` |
| `MultimodalEmbedding` | `multimodalembedding` |

On Vertex AI, the SDK sends Gemini and model-as-a-service embedding models to `embedContent`/`batchEmbedContents`.
It sends other text embedding models, such as `text-embedding-005`, gecko and multilingual, to `predict`.

### `VertexAIModels.Imagen` (retired)

Vertex AI retired all Imagen models on June 30, 2026, and the whole class is `[Obsolete]`. Google's recommended
replacement is a Gemini image model, such as `VertexAIModels.Gemini.GeminiNanoBanana21` or `Gemini3ProImage`. The
retired constants are `Imagen4Generate001`, `Imagen4UltraGenerate001`, `Imagen4FastGenerate001`, `Imagen4GeneratePreview0606`,
`Imagen4UltraGeneratePreview0606`, `Imagen3Generate001`, `Imagen3FastGenerate001`, `Imagen3Generate002`,
`Imagen3Capability001` (editing and customization), and `ImageGeneration006`/`005`/`002`.
Their IDs are the same strings without a prefix, for example `imagen-4.0-generate-001`.

### `VertexAIModels.Video`

`Veo2Generate001`, `Veo3Generate001`, `Veo3FastGenerate001`, `Veo3GeneratePreview`, `Veo3FastGeneratePreview`,
`Veo31GeneratePreview` and `Veo31FastGeneratePreview`. For example, `Veo31GeneratePreview` is `veo-3.1-generate-preview`.

### Other

- `VertexAIModels.Gemma`: `GemmaModel` (`gemma`), `CodeGemma` (`codegemma`), `PaliGemma` (`paligemma`)
- `VertexAIModels.Codey`: `CodeGecko` (`code-gecko`)
- `VertexAIModels.MedLM`: `MedLMMedium` (`medlm-medium`), `MedLMLarge` (`medlm-large`)

## Deprecated and shut-down constants

The SDK keeps these `GoogleAIModels` constants so existing code still compiles. They are marked
`[Obsolete(..., false)]`, which means using one gives compiler warning CS0618, not an error.
The replacements below come from the attribute messages.

### Deprecated, but still served for now

| Constant | Status | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `Gemini25Flash` | Deprecated; from Dec 1, 2026 requests are routed to gemini-3.5-flash-lite | `Gemini38Flash` or `Gemini35FlashLite` |
| `Gemini25Pro` | Deprecated; from Dec 1, 2026 requests are routed to gemini-3.8-flash | `Gemini38Flash` or a Gemini 4 model |
| `Gemini25FlashPreviewTts`, `Gemini25ProPreviewTts` | Shutdown Dec 18, 2026 | `Gemini38FlashTts` |
| `GeminiEmbeddingExp` | Deprecated | `GeminiEmbedding2` or `GeminiEmbedding` |
| `Embedding` (`models/embedding-001`) | Older model | `GeminiEmbedding2` or `GeminiEmbedding` |
| `Aqa` | No longer in Google's docs | See [Legacy Semantic Retrieval (AQA)](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Legacy-Semantic-Retrieval-(AQA)) |

### Shut down or no longer listed

| Constant(s) | Status | Use instead |
|---|---|---|
| `Gemini3ProPreview` | Shut down Mar 9, 2026 | `Gemini31ProPreview` or a Gemini 4 model |
| `Gemini3ProImagePreview` | Shut down Jun 25, 2026 | `Gemini3ProImage` |
| `Gemini2Flash`, `Gemini2FlashLatest` | Shut down Jun 1, 2026 | `Gemini38Flash` |
| `Gemini2FlashLite` | Shut down Jun 1, 2026 | `Gemini35FlashLite` |
| `Gemini2FlashLitePreview` | Shut down Dec 9, 2025 | `Gemini35FlashLite` |
| `Gemini2FlashExp`, `Gemini2FlashThinkingExp0121`, `Gemini25FlashPreview0417` | No longer listed | `Gemini38Flash` |
| `Gemini25ProPreview0520`, `Gemini25FlashPreview092025` | Shut down | `Gemini38Flash` |
| `Gemini25FlashLitePreview092025`, `Gemini25FlashLitePreview0617` | Shut down / no longer listed | `Gemini35FlashLite` (or `Gemini25FlashLite`) |
| `Gemini25ProExp0325`, `Gemini25ProPreview0325`, `Gemini25ProPreview0506`, `Gemini25ProPreview0605` | Shut down / no longer listed | A Gemini 4 model |
| `Gemini2FlashLive001`, `GeminiLive25FlashPreview`, `Gemini25FlashLivePreview`, `Gemini25FlashNativeAudioLatest`, `Gemini25FlashPreviewNativeAudioDialog` | Shut down / no longer listed | `Gemini38Live` |
| `Gemini25FlashNativeAudioPreview092025` | No longer listed | `Gemini38Live` or `Gemini25FlashNativeAudioPreview122025` |
| `Gemini25FlashPreviewNativeAudioThinkingDialog` | No longer listed | `Gemini38LiveExtendedThinking` |

| `Gemini2FlashExpImageGeneration`, `Gemini2FlashPreviewImageGeneration` | Shut down / no longer listed | `GeminiNanoBanana21` |
| `Gemini25ComputerUsePreview102025` | Shut down Jul 28, 2026 | Computer Use is now a GA tool on current Gemini models |
| `GeminiRoboticsEr15Preview` | Shut down Apr 30, 2026 | `GeminiRoboticsEr2Preview` |
| `TextEmbedding` (`models/text-embedding-004`) | Shut down Jan 14, 2026 | `GeminiEmbedding2` or `GeminiEmbedding` |

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Migration-Guide-v4 -->

# Migrating from v3.x to v4.0

v4.0.0 mostly adds features. Most apps only need to update the package and replace model IDs that Google has retired.
This page lists everything that can change how your code builds or runs.

For the full list of new features, see [Release Notes v4](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Release-Notes-v4).

---

## 1. Update the packages

All packages move to **4.0.0** together:

```bash
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI --version 4.0.0
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft --version 4.0.0   # if you use Microsoft.Extensions.AI
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Tools --version 4.0.0       # if you use MCP or function tools
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Live --version 4.0.0        # if you use the Live API
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Web --version 4.0.0
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Auth --version 4.0.0
```

### Target frameworks

| Package | v3.6.9 | v4.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Google_GenerativeAI, .Auth | net6.0, net7.0, net8.0, net9.0, netstandard2.0, net462 | + **net10.0**, **net11.0** |
| Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft, .Tools | net8.0, net9.0, netstandard2.0, net462 | + **net10.0**, **net11.0** |
| Google_GenerativeAI.Web | net6.0, net7.0, net8.0, net9.0, netstandard2.0 | + **net10.0**, **net11.0** |
| Google_GenerativeAI.Live | net6.0, net7.0, net8.0, net9.0 | + **net10.0**, **net11.0** |

net11.0 assets are built only when the .NET 11 SDK is installed on the build machine.

### Dependency versions (may affect your own package references)

| Dependency | v3.6.9 | v4.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft.Extensions.Logging / System.Text.Json | 9.0.3 (net8/net9/netstandard2.0/net462) | **10.0.15** on net8.0/net9.0; **11.0.0** on net10.0+, netstandard2.0, net462 (net10+ uses the in-box System.Text.Json); net6/net7 unchanged (8.x) |
| Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration/Options/DependencyInjection.Abstractions (Web, Live) | 9.0.10 | **10.0.15** on net8.0/net9.0; **11.0.0** on net10.0+ and netstandard2.0; 9.0.10 on net6/net7 |
| Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions | 9.10.0 | **10.11.0** on net8.0/net9.0; **11.0.0** on all other targets |
| ModelContextProtocol / ModelContextProtocol.Core | 0.4.0-preview.3 | **2.4.0** |
| CSharpToJsonSchema | 3.10.2-dev.69 | 3.10.6 |
| Microsoft.Bcl.Memory (Tools) | transitive | 10.0.15 (net8/net9) / 11.0.0 |
| Websocket.Client (Live) | 5.3.0 | 5.5.1 |
| Google.Apis.Auth (Auth) | 1.72.0 | 1.78.0 |

What to check:

- **Microsoft.Extensions.AI:** if your app references `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` or `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions`
  directly, use the same major version the SDK uses for your target framework: 10.x on net8/net9, 11.x on net10+.
  Mixed MEAI versions cause `MissingMethodException` at runtime.
- **MCP:** ModelContextProtocol went from a 0.4 preview to 2.x. `McpTool` and `McpTransportFactory` work as before.
  If you use types from the MCP SDK directly, such as `McpClient`, `IClientTransport` or `StdioClientTransportOptions`,
  check the MCP SDK's own breaking changes. `McpTransportFactory.CreateHttpTransport*` now also has `Uri` overloads;
  the `string` overloads still work.

---

## 2. Breaking changes

### 2.1 Subclasses of `BaseModel`: embedding methods take a `CancellationToken`

The protected virtual embedding methods gained a `CancellationToken` parameter. Code that calls them still compiles,
because the parameter is optional. **Overrides must be updated:**

```csharp
// v3.x
protected override Task<EmbedContentResponse> EmbedContentAsync(string model, EmbedContentRequest request) { ... }
protected override Task<BatchEmbedContentsResponse> BatchEmbedContentAsync(string model, BatchEmbedContentRequest request) { ... }

// v4.0
protected override Task<EmbedContentResponse> EmbedContentAsync(string model, EmbedContentRequest request,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
protected override Task<BatchEmbedContentsResponse> BatchEmbedContentAsync(string model, BatchEmbedContentRequest request,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
```

Libraries compiled against v3.x that override or call these methods must be recompiled.

### 2.2 Function results are sent with the `user` role

Gemini 3.x models reject the legacy `function` role with `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Like the official SDKs, v4 sends
function results with role `user`:

- `FunctionCallExtensions.ToFunctionCallContent(...)` now returns `Content` with `Role = Roles.User`.
- `GenerativeModel` converts any `Content` with `Role == "function"` to `"user"` before sending. Chat histories
  saved by older versions keep working.
- With Microsoft.Extensions.AI, a turn made up only of function responses still converts back to `ChatRole.Tool`.

If your code finds function-result turns by checking `content.Role == Roles.Function`, check the parts instead:

```csharp
// v3.x
var isFunctionResult = content.Role == Roles.Function;

// v4.0
var isFunctionResult = content.Parts.Count > 0 && content.Parts.All(p => p.FunctionResponse != null);
```

### 2.3 Default model changed

`GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel` changed from `models/gemini-2.5-flash` to **`models/gemini-3.8-flash`**. Code that
creates a model without passing one (and without `GOOGLE_AI_MODEL`) now calls Gemini 3.8 Flash. Pass a model explicitly
if you need a specific one.

Other defaults changed to replace retired models:

| API | v3.x default | v4.0 default |
|---|---|---|
| `MicrosoftExtensions.AsEmbeddingGenerator(apiKey/adapter, modelName)` | `text-embedding-004` (shut down) | `GoogleAIModels.GeminiEmbedding` (`models/gemini-embedding-001`) |
| `GenerativeAIImageGenerator(apiKey/adapter, modelName)` | `Gemini25FlashImagePreview` (shut down) | `GoogleAIModels.GeminiNanoBanana21` |

### 2.4 Retired model constants now produce warnings

Constants for models that Google has shut down or deprecated are marked `[Obsolete(..., false)]`. Using one gives
compiler **warning CS0618**, which **breaks the build if you use `TreatWarningsAsErrors`**. Common replacements:

| v3.x constant | Use instead |
|---|---|
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini25Flash` | `Gemini38Flash` or `Gemini35FlashLite` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini25Pro` | `Gemini38Flash` or a Gemini 4 model (`Gemini4Hydrogen`, `Gemini4Carbon`, `Gemini4Argon`) |
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini2Flash` / `Gemini2FlashLatest` | `Gemini38Flash` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini2FlashLite` | `Gemini35FlashLite` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini3ProPreview` | `Gemini31ProPreview` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini2FlashLive001`, `GeminiLive25FlashPreview` | `Gemini38Live` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini25FlashImagePreview` | `GeminiNanoBanana21` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Gemini25FlashPreviewTts` / `Gemini25ProPreviewTts` | `Gemini38FlashTts` |
| `GoogleAIModels.TextEmbedding` (`text-embedding-004`) | `GeminiEmbedding2` or `GeminiEmbedding` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Imagen.Imagen4Generate001` (and other Imagen on the Gemini API) | `GeminiNanoBanana21` |
| `GoogleAIModels.Video.Veo*` | `GoogleAIModels.Video.GeminiOmni12Flash` through the Interactions API, or Veo on Vertex AI |
| `GoogleAIModels.Aqa` | [File Search](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/File-Search) or [Vertex RAG Engine](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Vertex-RAG-Engine) |

The full table is in [Supported Models](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Supported-Models#deprecated-and-shut-down-constants).
`GoogleAIModels.TextEmbedding` stays in `SupportedEmbedingModels.All`, so the SDK still accepts it, but Google's API
rejects it.

### 2.5 Veo on the Gemini API fails fast

Google retired Veo models on the Gemini API. `VideoGenerationModel` now throws `NotSupportedException` right away on
the Gemini API, without sending a request. Vertex AI is unchanged.

```csharp
// v3.x - request sent, rejected by the API
var video = new VideoGenerationModel(googleAiAdapter, GoogleAIModels.Video.Veo3Generate001);

// v4.0 - use Vertex AI for Veo...
var vertexVideo = new VideoGenerationModel(vertexAdapter, VertexAIModels.Video.Veo31GeneratePreview);
// ...or Gemini Omni on the Gemini API through the Interactions API (see Interactions-API / Video-Generation)
```

### 2.6 Live API message types match the wire format

`LiveServerGoAway` and `LiveServerSessionResumptionUpdate` in v3.x used field names the Live API never sends, so
those objects were always empty. The old properties still exist but are `[Obsolete]`:

| Old (always null) | New |
|---|---|
| `LiveServerSessionResumptionUpdate.ResumptionToken` | `NewHandle` |
| `LiveServerSessionResumptionUpdate.Status` (`SessionResumptionStatus`) | `Resumable` (`bool?`) |
| `LiveServerSessionResumptionUpdate.Message` | (none); also new: `LastConsumedClientMessageIndex` |
| `LiveServerGoAway.ErrorCode`, `ErrorMessage`, `Reconnect`, `RetryAfterSeconds` | `TimeLeft` (string, e.g. `"30s"`) and `TimeLeftDuration` (`TimeSpan?`) |

`SessionResumptionStatus` is also `[Obsolete]`. `MultiModalLiveClient.LastSessionResumptionHandle` now tracks the
latest handle for you.

#### Live API message types renamed to match the official SDKs

The `Bidi*` Live API message types now use the same names as the official Google GenAI SDKs (python-genai). Only
the .NET type names changed; the JSON sent over the WebSocket is identical. Rename any references in your code:

| v3.x | v4 |
|---|---|
| `BidiClientPayload` | `LiveClientMessage` |
| `BidiGenerateContentSetup` | `LiveClientSetup` |
| `BidiGenerateContentClientContent` | `LiveClientContent` |
| `BidiGenerateContentRealtimeInput` | `LiveClientRealtimeInput` |
| `BidiGenerateContentToolResponse` | `LiveClientToolResponse` |
| `BidiGenerateContentContextUpdate` | `LiveClientContextUpdate` |
| `BidiResponsePayload` | `LiveServerMessage` |
| `BidiGenerateContentServerContent` | `LiveServerContent` |
| `BidiGenerateContentSetupComplete` | `LiveServerSetupComplete` |
| `BidiGenerateContentToolCall` | `LiveServerToolCall` |
| `BidiGenerateContentToolCallCancellation` | `LiveServerToolCallCancellation` |

The most common change is in `MessageReceived` handlers, where `e.Payload` is now a `LiveServerMessage`.

### 2.7 Parameter rename on `IPlatformAdapter.GetBaseUrl`

`GetBaseUrl(bool appendVesion, ...)` was renamed to `GetBaseUrl(bool appendVersion, ...)`. Only callers that pass
the argument **by name** (`appendVesion: false`) need to change.

### 2.8 `apiVersion` parameters are nullable

`GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(..., string? apiVersion = null, ...)` and `VertextPlatformAdapter(..., string? apiVersion = null, ...)`
used to default to `ApiVersions.v1Beta` and `ApiVersions.v1Beta1`. These are still the defaults unless the new
`GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION` environment variable is set. Your source code doesn't need to change. Recompile anything
that binds to these constructors. See [Configuration and Error Handling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Configuration-and-Error-Handling).

---

## 3. Behaviour changes (no code change required)

| Area | v3.x | v4.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Error handling | Streaming requests and file uploads threw a bare `HttpRequestException`. Array-shaped error bodies (`[{"error":...}]`) were not parsed | All requests throw `ApiException` with `ErrorCode`/`ErrorStatus`/`ErrorMessage`. Array bodies are parsed, and the HTTP status is used when the body has no code. Non-Google bodies give an `HttpRequestException` with the status and a truncated body. **If you caught `HttpRequestException` around streaming or uploads, also catch `ApiException`.** |
| `generateContent` continuation | Responses that Google ended early with a continuation token came back incomplete | Followed automatically and merged. Turn off with `GenerativeModel.EnableAutomaticContinuation = false`. Limited by `MaxContinuations` (10) |
| Embedding model validation | Exact string match, so `gemini-embedding-001` without `models/` failed | Compares bare IDs: `models/x`, `publishers/google/models/x` and `x` all pass |
| Embedding cancellation | `EmbeddingModel` ignored the `CancellationToken` | Token passed through to the HTTP request |
| Vertex AI embeddings | Gemini API request format sent to Vertex, so `taskType`, `title` and `outputDimensionality` were ignored, and `text-embedding-005`/gecko failed | Vertex format: `embedContent` with `embedContentConfig` for Gemini models, `predict` for text embedding models. New Vertex-only options `AutoTruncate`, `DocumentOcr`, `AudioTrackExtraction`, `MimeType` (throw `NotSupportedException` on the Gemini API) |
| `VertextPlatformAdapter(validateAccessToken: ...)` | Argument ignored | Honoured |
| Vertex batch cancel | `BatchClient.CancelAsync` called the job URL without the `:cancel` suffix, so jobs were not cancelled | Calls `{job name}:cancel` |
| `VertexRagManager.AwaitForLongRunningOperation(id, timeOut)` | `timeOut` ignored (always `LongRunningOperationTimeout`) | `timeOut` honoured. Failed operations report the error code |
| `AddGenerativeAI(GenerativeAIOptions)` | `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` in the environment switched to Vertex AI even when you passed only an API key | An API key with no `ProjectId` (and no `IsVertex`/`ExpressMode`) means the Gemini API |
| Microsoft.Extensions.AI chat client | The model's function-call turn was added once per call, which broke parallel calls. Streaming only looked for function calls in the last chunk | Fixed: one model turn, and parts collected across the whole stream |
| `RemoteFileContent` (MEAI) | Sent an empty file URI when the remote file had none | Throws `InvalidOperationException` ("upload the file before referencing it") |
| `MultiModalLiveClient` | Exceptions in the message handler (including your event handlers) could crash the process. Reconnects didn't re-send setup. `SafetySettings` were not sent | Exceptions go to `ErrorOccurred`. Setup is re-sent after a reconnect, resuming with the last handle (`ResendSetupOnReconnect`, default `true`). `SafetySettings` are sent. New `TurnCompleted` event |
| Imagen through MEAI (`GenerativeAIImagenGenerator`) | Default `Imagen3Generate002` | `[Obsolete]`: every Imagen model is retired (Vertex AI on June 30, 2026). Use `GenerativeAIImageGenerator`, which defaults to `GeminiNanoBanana21` |

---

## 4. Moved to "legacy"

Google no longer documents **Semantic Retrieval / AQA** (`SemanticRetrieverModel`, `CorporaManager`, `CorporaClient`,
`DocumentsClient`, `ChunkClient`, `CorpusPermissionClient`). The APIs still work in v4, but `GoogleAIModels.Aqa` is
`[Obsolete]`. Their wiki pages are merged into [Legacy Semantic Retrieval (AQA)](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Legacy-Semantic-Retrieval-(AQA)).
For new work, use [File Search](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/File-Search) (Gemini API) or the [Vertex RAG Engine](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Vertex-RAG-Engine).

---

## 5. Checklist

- [ ] Update all `Google_GenerativeAI*` packages to 4.0.0 together.
- [ ] Align any direct `Microsoft.Extensions.AI*` and `ModelContextProtocol` references with the versions above.
- [ ] Fix CS0618 warnings by moving to current model constants ([Supported Models](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Supported-Models)).
- [ ] Update `EmbedContentAsync`/`BatchEmbedContentAsync` overrides to take a `CancellationToken`.
- [ ] Replace `Role == Roles.Function` checks with checks on `FunctionResponse` parts.
- [ ] Catch `ApiException` (not only `HttpRequestException`) around streaming and file uploads.
- [ ] Move Veo calls on the Gemini API to Vertex AI or Gemini Omni, and Imagen on the Gemini API to Gemini image models.
- [ ] Live API: read `NewHandle`/`Resumable`/`TimeLeft` instead of the obsolete properties.
- [ ] Vertex AI: use `region: "global"` for the newest Gemini models.


---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Release-Notes-v4 -->

# Release Notes: v4.0.0

v4.0.0 adds support for the current Gemini API and Vertex AI: new APIs, current model IDs, .NET 10/11 targets, and
updated dependencies. Upgrading from 3.x? Read the [Migration Guide v4](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Migration-Guide-v4) first.

Previous release: 3.6.9.

---

## Highlights

- **New APIs:** [Interactions](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Interactions-API), [File Search](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/File-Search), [Webhooks](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Webhooks), ephemeral Live API
  tokens, [Model Tuning](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Model-Tuning), [Live Music](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Live-API), and the [Agent APIs](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Agent-APIs)
  (Agents, Environments, Triggers, Credentials, Decisions, Voices).
- **Current models:** Gemini 4, Gemini 3.x, Gemini 3.8 Live and TTS, Nano Banana 2.1, Gemini Omni video, Lyria and
  Gemini Embedding 2. Retired models are marked `[Obsolete]` with their replacements. See [Supported Models](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Supported-Models).
- **Default model is now `gemini-3.8-flash`.**
- **.NET 10 and .NET 11** target frameworks.
- **Better errors:** Google error details come back as `ApiException` for every request, including streaming and
  file uploads.
- **Automatic continuation:** `generateContent` and Interactions follow continuation tokens on their own.

---

## New features

### Interactions API ([Interactions-API](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Interactions-API))
- `InteractionsClient` (`GenAI.CreateInteractionsClient()`): `CreateAsync`, `StreamAsync`, `GetAsync`,
  `ResumeStreamAsync`, `CancelAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `WaitForCompletionAsync`, `ContinueAsync`.
- Follows `requires_continuation` automatically (`EnableAutomaticContinuation`, `MaxContinuations` = 10). Background
  interactions are not continued.
- Resumes a dropped stream from the last event (`MaxStreamReconnects` = 3).
- Agent model constants: `GoogleAIModels.Agents.DeepResearchPreview042026`, `DeepResearchMaxPreview042026`,
  `AntigravityPreview092026`.

### File Search ([File-Search](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/File-Search))
- `FileSearchStoresClient` (`GoogleAi.CreateFileSearchStoresClient()`): create, get, list and delete stores; upload
  files or streams; import from the Files API; manage documents and operations; download media.
- `GenerativeModel.UseFileSearch(...)` and the new `Tool.FileSearch` tool, plus `ChunkingConfig` and grounding
  metadata for retrieved context.

### Webhooks ([Webhooks](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Webhooks))
- `WebhooksClient` (`GenAI.CreateWebhooksClient()`): create, get, list, update, delete, ping and rotate the signing secret.
- `BatchClient.CreateAsync(model, source, destination, webhookConfig, ...)` sends a per-job `WebhookConfig`. This works
  on the Gemini API only; Vertex AI throws `NotSupportedException`. See [Batch API](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Batch-API).

### Live API ([Multimodal-Live-API](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Live-API))
- **Ephemeral auth tokens:** `AuthTokensClient.CreateAsync(CreateAuthTokenConfig)` (Gemini API, `v1alpha`). When you
  pass an `auth_tokens/...` token as the key, `MultiModalLiveClient` connects to the constrained endpoint, so client
  apps don't need the API key.
- New client methods: `SendRealtimeInputAsync`, `SendVideoFrameAsync`, `SendRealtimeTextAsync`,
  `SendActivityStartAsync`/`SendActivityEndAsync` (manual voice activity detection), `SendAudioStreamEndAsync`, and
  `SendContextUpdateAsync` (change the system instruction or tools during a session).
- New setup options: `RealtimeInputConfig`, `SessionResumption`, `ContextWindowCompression`, `Proactivity`,
  `HistoryConfig`, input/output audio transcription configs, and translation.
- Reconnects re-send setup and resume the session (`ResendSetupOnReconnect`, `LastSessionResumptionHandle`).
  New `TurnCompleted` event. Exceptions in handlers go to `ErrorOccurred`.
- **Live Music (Lyria RealTime):** `LiveMusicClient` with `SetWeightedPromptsAsync`, `SetMusicGenerationConfigAsync`,
  `PlayAsync`/`PauseAsync`/`StopAsync`/`ResetContextAsync` (Gemini API).

### Model tuning ([Model-Tuning](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Model-Tuning))
- `TuningClient` (`GenAI.CreateTuningClient()`): tune, get, list, cancel, wait for completion, and validate rewards.
  Covers Vertex AI tuning jobs (supervised, preference, distillation, reinforcement, Veo LoRA) and Gemini API tuned models.
- `ModelClient.UpdateModelAsync`, `DeleteModelAsync`, and Vertex `ComputeTokensAsync`.
- `FileClient.DownloadFileAsync` and `RegisterFilesAsync`.

### Agent APIs ([Agent-APIs](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Agent-APIs))
- `AgentsClient`, `EnvironmentsClient` (including workspace file upload and download), `TriggersClient`
  (create, update, pause, resume, run, executions, `WaitForExecutionAsync`), `CredentialsClient`, `DecisionsClient`
  (`gemini-decision-1`), and `VoicesClient` (design, remix and replicate voices). All are created from `GenAI` factory
  methods (`CreateAgentsClient()` and so on).

### Vertex RAG Engine ([Vertex-RAG-Engine](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Vertex-RAG-Engine))
- `VertexRagManager.GetEngineConfigAsync`, `UpdateEngineConfigAsync` and `SwitchToServerlessModeAsync`
  (`RagEngineConfig`, `RagManagedDbConfig.CreateServerless()`).
- RAG operation errors now include the error code.

### Generation, tools and configuration
- **Automatic continuation** in `GenerateContentAsync` and `StreamContentAsync` (`GenerativeModel.EnableAutomaticContinuation`,
  `MaxContinuations`). See [Configuration and Error Handling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Configuration-and-Error-Handling).
- **`GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION`** environment variable sets the default API version (`beta` means `v1beta`/`v1beta1`).
  `ApiVersions.v1Alpha` added.
- **Structured error parsing:** both object and array error bodies, the HTTP status used when the body has no code, and
  consistent `ApiException` for streaming and uploads.
- New request and config fields: `ServiceTier` (`ServiceTiers.Standard`/`Flex`/`Priority`), `Store`, `Labels`,
  `ContinuationToken`, `ModelArmorConfig`, `ResponseFormat`, per-part media resolution, image output options
  (`PersonGeneration`, `OutputMimeType`, `OutputCompressionQuality`), `AudioTranscriptionConfig` and `TranslationConfig`.
- New tools: `FileSearch`, `McpServers` (server-side MCP), `ParallelAiSearch`, `ExaAiSearch`, plus updated Google
  Search, Google Maps, Computer Use and Vertex tool options.
- New response fields: finish and block reasons, model status, traffic type, and server-side tool invocations.

### Embeddings ([Embeddings](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Embeddings))
- `GeminiEmbedding2` added. The SDK accepts prefixed model IDs (`models/...`, `publishers/google/models/...`).
- Vertex AI embeddings use Vertex's request format (`embedContent` or `predict`). New Vertex-only options:
  `AutoTruncate`, `DocumentOcr`, `AudioTrackExtraction`, `MimeType`.
- `CancellationToken` is passed through to the HTTP request.

### Image and video generation ([Image-Generation](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Image-Generation), [Video-Generation](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Video-Generation))
- Gemini image models: `GeminiNanoBanana21`, `Gemini31FlashImage`, `Gemini31FlashLiteImage`, `Gemini3ProImage`.
  `GenerativeAIImageGenerator` now defaults to Nano Banana 2.1.
- Video on the Gemini API: Gemini Omni (`GoogleAIModels.Video.GeminiOmni12Flash`) through the Interactions API.

### Context caching ([Context-Caching](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Context-Caching))
- No API changes. Docs and samples now use current model IDs.

---

## Model and platform changes

- **Imagen retired:** Google retired Imagen on the Gemini API and, on June 30, 2026, on Vertex AI. `ImagenModel`, `GenAI.CreateImageModel`, `GenerativeAIImagenGenerator` and the Imagen model constants are marked `[Obsolete]`; use the Gemini image models and `GenerativeAIImageGenerator`.
- **Veo retired on the Gemini API:** `VideoGenerationModel` now throws `NotSupportedException` on the Gemini API. Use
  Veo on Vertex AI or Gemini Omni.
- **Retired and deprecated model constants** are `[Obsolete]` with replacement guidance. `text-embedding-004`, the
  Gemini 2.0 family, Gemini 2.5 previews, and Gemini 3 Pro Preview are shut down. `gemini-2.5-flash` and
  `gemini-2.5-pro` are deprecated, and from December 1, 2026 Google routes them to newer models.
- **Semantic Retrieval / AQA** is now legacy. See [Legacy Semantic Retrieval (AQA)](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Legacy-Semantic-Retrieval-(AQA)).
- Google deprecated `temperature`, `topP` and `topK` for Gemini 3.6+ models. The SDK never sets them on its own.
- Vertex AI: Google serves the newest Gemini models from the `global` location.

---

## Fixes

- Function results are sent with the `user` role. Gemini 3.x rejects `function`, and old histories are converted
  automatically.
- Microsoft.Extensions.AI chat client: fixed duplicated model turns with parallel function calls (which gave empty
  answers), and streaming function calls in chunks before the last one are no longer missed.
- `AsEmbeddingGenerator()` defaulted to the shut-down `text-embedding-004`. It now uses `gemini-embedding-001`.
- Vertex batch cancel now calls `:cancel`.
- `VertexRagManager.AwaitForLongRunningOperation` honours `timeOut`.
- `VertextPlatformAdapter` honours `validateAccessToken`.
- `AddGenerativeAI(options)` with only an API key no longer switches to Vertex AI because `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` is set.
- Live API: `GoAway` and session resumption messages now match the wire format. `SendSetupAsync` sends `SafetySettings`.
  Reconnection disposes old sockets.
- `RemoteFileContent` without a URI throws instead of sending an empty file URI.
- Fixed all 277 build warnings across target frameworks. Resolved open Dependabot vulnerability alerts.

---

## Breaking changes (summary)

See the [Migration Guide v4](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Migration-Guide-v4) for code samples.

1. `BaseModel.EmbedContentAsync`/`BatchEmbedContentAsync` (protected virtual) now take a `CancellationToken`. Overrides must be updated.
2. Function-result `Content` uses `Roles.User` instead of `Roles.Function`.
3. `DefaultGeminiModel` changed to `gemini-3.8-flash`. The default models for `AsEmbeddingGenerator` and `GenerativeAIImageGenerator` changed.
4. Retired model constants are `[Obsolete]` (warning CS0618).
5. Veo on the Gemini API throws `NotSupportedException`.
6. Live API: the old `GoAway` and session resumption properties are `[Obsolete]`. Use `TimeLeft`, `NewHandle` and `Resumable`.
7. `IPlatformAdapter.GetBaseUrl` parameter renamed from `appendVesion` to `appendVersion`.
8. Streaming and upload errors throw `ApiException` instead of `HttpRequestException` when the body is a Google error.
9. Dependencies: Microsoft.Extensions.* 10.x/11.x, Microsoft.Extensions.AI 10.11/11.0, ModelContextProtocol 2.4.0.

---

## Dependencies and target frameworks

- Added **net10.0** to all packages. **net11.0** is added when the package is built with the .NET 11 SDK.
- Microsoft.Extensions.* and System.Text.Json: 10.0.15 on net8.0/net9.0; 11.0.0 on net10.0+, netstandard2.0 and net462.
- Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions: 10.11.0 on net8.0/net9.0; 11.0.0 elsewhere.
- ModelContextProtocol 2.4.0, CSharpToJsonSchema 3.10.6, Websocket.Client 5.5.1, Google.Apis.Auth 1.78.0.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Generate-Content -->

This page shows how to generate content with `GenerativeModel`. You can call one of the convenience `GenerateContentAsync` overloads, or build a `GenerateContentRequest` yourself for full control. It also covers generation config, thinking, token counting, automatic continuation and error handling.

Package: `Google_GenerativeAI`. For setup, see [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization).

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var model = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY").CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
```

## Method 1: Convenience Overloads

### `GenerateContentAsync(string prompt)`

```csharp
GenerateContentResponse response = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Write a short poem about nature.");
Console.WriteLine(response.Text());
```

### `GenerateContentAsync(string prompt, string fileUri, string mimeType)`

Sends a prompt together with a **remote file URI**, such as a Files API URI, a `gs://` URI on Vertex AI or a public URL the model can fetch. To send a local file, see [Multimodal Features](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Features).

```csharp
var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(
    "Describe the image.",
    "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/files/abc123",
    "image/jpeg");
Console.WriteLine(response.Text());
```

### `GenerateContentAsync(IEnumerable<Part> parts)`

All parts are sent in a single `user` turn:

```csharp
var parts = new List<Part>
{
    new Part { Text = "What are the benefits of using cloud computing?" },
    new Part { Text = "Answer in three bullet points." }
};

var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(parts);
Console.WriteLine(response.Text());
```

All overloads accept an optional `CancellationToken`.

## Method 2: Building a `GenerateContentRequest`

Use the extension methods on `GenerateContentRequest` to add text, parts, files, tools and JSON mode:

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();

// Text (appended to the last content, or a new user content if there is none)
request.AddText("Summarize the following article: ...");

// Parts
request.AddParts(new List<Part> { new Part { Text = "Keep it under 100 words." } });

// A whole Content with an explicit role
request.AddContent(new Content("Here is some more context.", Roles.User));

// Files
request.AddInlineFile("chart.png");                            // local file, sent inline (base64)
request.AddRemoteFile("https://example.com/report.pdf", "application/pdf");

// Tools (see Function Calling)
request.AddTool(new Tool { GoogleSearch = new GoogleSearchTool() });

// Generation settings
request.GenerationConfig = new GenerationConfig
{
    Temperature = 0.7,
    MaxOutputTokens = 1024
};

GenerateContentResponse response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
Console.WriteLine(response.Text());
```

To get structured output, call `request.UseJsonMode<MyResponseClass>()` or use `GenerateObjectAsync<T>`. See [JSON Mode](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Json-Mode).

### Request fields

| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| `Contents` | Conversation turns (`List<Content>`) |
| `SystemInstruction` | A `Content` with system instructions |
| `GenerationConfig` | Sampling, output and thinking settings |
| `SafetySettings` | Per-request `List<SafetySetting>` |
| `Tools`, `ToolConfig` | Function declarations, Google Search, code execution, ... |
| `CachedContent` | Name of a context cache (see [Context Caching](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Context-Caching)) |
| `ContinuationToken` | Resumes a response that ended with `FinishReason.CONTINUATION` (normally handled for you) |
| `ServiceTier`, `Store`, `Labels`, `ModelArmorConfig`, `OutputConfig` | Optional API features |

Request values take precedence. When a request doesn't set `GenerationConfig`, `SafetySettings` or `SystemInstruction`, the model's own `Config`, `SafetySettings` and `SystemInstruction` are used.

## Model-Level Defaults

```csharp
var model = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY").CreateGenerativeModel(
    GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash,
    config: new GenerationConfig { Temperature = 0.4 },
    systemInstruction: "You are a helpful technical writer.");

// Or set them later
model.SystemInstruction = "Answer in French.";
model.Config = new GenerationConfig { MaxOutputTokens = 512 };
```

## Generation Config

Commonly used `GenerationConfig` properties:

| Property | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Temperature`, `TopP`, `TopK`, `Seed` | Sampling |
| `MaxOutputTokens`, `StopSequences`, `CandidateCount` | Output length and stop conditions |
| `PresencePenalty`, `FrequencyPenalty` | Repetition control |
| `ResponseMimeType`, `ResponseSchema`, `ResponseJsonSchema` | Structured output (see [JSON Mode](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Json-Mode)) |
| `ResponseModalities` | Ask for text, image or audio output |
| `ThinkingConfig` | Thinking budget, level and thought summaries |
| `MediaResolution` | Resolution used for image and video input |
| `SpeechConfig`, `ImageConfig` | Speech and image generation options |
| `ResponseLogprobs`, `Logprobs` | Return log probabilities |

## Thinking

Gemini 3.x models use a **thinking level**. Gemini 2.5 models use a **thinking budget** in tokens. Set `IncludeThoughts` to receive thought summaries.

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddText("How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 100?");
request.GenerationConfig = new GenerationConfig
{
    ThinkingConfig = new ThinkingConfig
    {
        ThinkingLevel = ThinkingLevel.HIGH,   // MINIMAL, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, XHIGH (model dependent)
        IncludeThoughts = true
        // ThinkingBudget = 1024,             // Gemini 2.5: thinking budget in tokens
    }
};

var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);

foreach (var part in response.Candidates![0].Content!.Parts)
{
    if (part.Thought == true)
        Console.WriteLine($"[thought] {part.Text}");
    else
        Console.WriteLine(part.Text);
}

Console.WriteLine($"Thinking tokens: {response.UsageMetadata?.ThoughtsTokenCount}");
```

> `response.Text()` joins the text of **all** parts, including thought summaries when `IncludeThoughts` is on. To get only the answer, filter on `Part.Thought` as shown above.

## Reading the Response

```csharp
var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Hello");

string? text = response.Text();          // extension: text of all candidates' parts
string last  = response.Text;            // property: text of the last candidate's parts
var finish   = response.Candidates?[0].FinishReason;
var usage    = response.UsageMetadata;   // PromptTokenCount, CandidatesTokenCount, TotalTokenCount, ...
var calls    = response.GetFunctions();  // function calls requested by the model, if any
var code     = response.ExtractCodeBlocks();
```

If the prompt is blocked, or the response has no candidates and carries a block reason, the SDK throws `GenerativeAIException` with the block details.

## Counting Tokens

```csharp
CountTokensResponse count = await model.CountTokensAsync(new[] { new Content("How long is this prompt?", Roles.User) });
Console.WriteLine(count.TotalTokens);

// A full request (including system instruction and tools)
var countForRequest = await model.CountTokensAsync(request);
```

On Vertex AI, `ModelClient.ComputeTokensAsync` also returns the individual tokens. See [Model Client](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Model-Client).

## Automatic Continuation

Some long responses end with `FinishReason.CONTINUATION` and a `Candidate.ContinuationToken`. By default, `GenerativeModel` resumes these responses automatically and merges the parts into one response. Streaming works the same way: a stream that fails after a checkpoint is resumed too.

```csharp
model.EnableAutomaticContinuation = true; // default
model.MaxContinuations = 10;              // default

// To handle it yourself:
model.EnableAutomaticContinuation = false;
var first = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
if (first.Candidates?[0].FinishReason == FinishReason.CONTINUATION)
{
    request.ContinuationToken = first.Candidates[0].ContinuationToken;
    var next = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
}
```

## Function Results Use the `user` Role

Gemini 3.x models reject the legacy `function` role. Before each request, the SDK rewrites any content with `Roles.Function` to `Roles.User`. This also fixes chat histories saved by older SDK versions. When you build function responses by hand, use `Roles.User`. See [Function Calling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Function-Calling).

## Error Handling

When the API returns an error, the SDK throws `GenerativeAI.Exceptions.ApiException`:

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Exceptions;

try
{
    var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Hello");
}
catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.ErrorCode == 429)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Rate limited ({ex.ErrorStatus}): {ex.ErrorMessage}");
}
catch (ApiException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{ex.ErrorCode} {ex.ErrorStatus}: {ex.ErrorMessage}");
}
catch (GenerativeAIException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Blocked: {ex.Details}");
}
```

If an error body can't be parsed, the SDK throws `HttpRequestException` with the status code and a short excerpt of the body.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Chat-Session -->

A `ChatSession` keeps the conversation history for you, so each new message is sent with the earlier turns. You send messages with the same `GenerateContentAsync` and `StreamContentAsync` methods you use on a model. `ChatSession` derives from `GenerativeModel`.

Package: `Google_GenerativeAI`. Setup: [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization).

## Creating a Chat Session

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var model = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY").CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
ChatSession chat = model.StartChat();
```

`StartChat` accepts these optional parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `history` | `List<Content>` to start from. Empty when omitted. |
| `config` | `GenerationConfig` for the session. Defaults to the model's `Config`. |
| `safetySettings` | `ICollection<SafetySetting>`. Defaults to the model's settings. |
| `systemInstruction` | System prompt for the session. Defaults to the model's `SystemInstruction`. |

The session also copies the model's function tools and its Google Search, code execution and retrieval settings.

### With history

```csharp
var history = new List<Content>
{
    new Content("Hello!", Roles.User),
    new Content("Hi there! How can I help you?", Roles.Model)
};

ChatSession chat = model.StartChat(history: history);
```

### With configuration and a system instruction

```csharp
ChatSession chat = model.StartChat(
    config: new GenerationConfig { Temperature = 0.8, MaxOutputTokens = 500 },
    systemInstruction: "You are a friendly travel guide.");
```

## Sending Messages

### `GenerateContentAsync`

```csharp
var chat = model.StartChat();

var response = await chat.GenerateContentAsync("What is the capital of France?");
Console.WriteLine($"Assistant: {response.Text()}");

response = await chat.GenerateContentAsync("And what is its population?");
Console.WriteLine($"Assistant: {response.Text()}");
```

### `StreamContentAsync`

```csharp
var chat = model.StartChat();

await foreach (var chunk in chat.StreamContentAsync("Tell me a story."))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}

// Or with a request
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddText("Now make it shorter.");

await foreach (var chunk in chat.StreamContentAsync(request))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}
```

When a stream finishes, the session joins the streamed text into one `model` turn and adds it to the history.

### Images and files in a chat

Build a request with a file and send it through the session:

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddInlineFile("image.png");
request.AddText("Identify the objects in this image.");

var first = await chat.GenerateContentAsync(request);
var followUp = await chat.GenerateContentAsync("Can you estimate the number of blueberries?");
```

See [Multimodal Features](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Features) for more ways to attach files.

## Inspecting and Editing History

```csharp
List<Content> turns = chat.History;          // alternating user / model turns
Content? lastUser   = chat.LastRequestContent;
Content? lastModel  = chat.LastResponseContent;

chat.History = new List<Content>();          // reset the conversation
```

Turns that only carry function calls or function results are not added to `History`. Only the final answer and the prompt that led to it are recorded.

## Saving and Restoring a Session

`CreateChatSessionBackUpData()` captures the history, config, safety settings, system instruction, model, cached content, JSON mode and tool settings. Pass the backup to `StartChat` to restore the session:

```csharp
using System.Text.Json;

ChatSessionBackUpData backup = chat.CreateChatSessionBackUpData();
string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(backup, DefaultSerializerOptions.Options);

// later...
var restoredBackup = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<ChatSessionBackUpData>(json, DefaultSerializerOptions.Options)!;
ChatSession restored = model.StartChat(restoredBackup);   // optional: pass List<IFunctionTool> tools
```

Function tools are code, so they aren't part of the backup. Pass them again through the `tools` parameter, or the session uses the model's `FunctionTools`.

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Streaming -->

Streaming returns a response in pieces while the model is still generating, so you can show text as it arrives. Every `StreamContentAsync` overload returns `IAsyncEnumerable<GenerateContentResponse>`, which you read with `await foreach`.

Package: `Google_GenerativeAI`. Setup: [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization).

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var model = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY").CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
```

## `StreamContentAsync` Overloads

### `StreamContentAsync(GenerateContentRequest request)`

This is the most general overload. Build the request as described in [Generate Content](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Generate-Content).

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddText("Write a story about a robot learning to love.");

await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync(request))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}
```

### `StreamContentAsync(string prompt)`

```csharp
await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync("Generate a list of 10 creative project ideas."))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}
```

### `StreamContentAsync(string prompt, string fileUri, string mimeType)`

Streams a response for a prompt and a **remote file URI**, such as a Files API URI, a `gs://` URI on Vertex AI or a public URL.

```csharp
await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync(
                   "Describe what is happening in this image.",
                   remoteFile.Uri!,           // e.g. from FileClient.UploadFileAsync
                   "image/jpeg"))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}
```

To stream with a **local file path**, use `GeminiModel.StreamContentAsync(prompt, filePath)`. See [Multimodal Features](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Features).

### `StreamContentAsync(IEnumerable<Part> parts)`

```csharp
var parts = new List<Part> { new Part { Text = "Translate 'Hello, world!' to Spanish." } };

await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync(parts))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}
```

### `StreamContentAsync(IEnumerable<Content> contents)`

```csharp
var contents = new List<Content>
{
    new Content("Explain the concept of quantum entanglement.", Roles.User)
};

await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync(contents))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}
```

## Cancellation

Every overload takes a `CancellationToken`. Pass it directly or use `WithCancellation`:

```csharp
using var cts = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30));

await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync("Write a long essay.", cts.Token))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}
```

## Collecting the Full Text

Each chunk holds only part of the output. Join the chunks to get the full text:

```csharp
var sb = new System.Text.StringBuilder();
await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync("Tell me a joke."))
{
    sb.Append(chunk.Text());
}
Console.WriteLine(sb.ToString());
```

## Behavior Notes

1. **Function calling**: When the last chunk asks for a function call and the model has function tools with auto-calling enabled, the SDK runs the function and keeps streaming the model's follow-up. See [Function Calling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Function-Calling).
2. **Automatic continuation**: If a stream ends with `FinishReason.CONTINUATION`, or fails after a continuation checkpoint, the SDK resumes it with the continuation token. This is controlled by `EnableAutomaticContinuation` and `MaxContinuations` (see [Generate Content](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Generate-Content#automatic-continuation)).
3. **Chat sessions**: `ChatSession.StreamContentAsync` adds the joined response to the history when the stream completes. See [Chat Session](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Chat-Session).
4. **Thinking**: With `ThinkingConfig.IncludeThoughts = true`, chunks can contain thought parts (`Part.Thought == true`).
5. **Errors**: An API error is thrown as `ApiException` while you iterate. Wrap the `await foreach` in `try`/`catch`.
