<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Features -->

Gemini models accept images, video, audio, PDFs and text files together with a text prompt. This page shows how to attach that media to a request: by local file path, inline data, an uploaded file or a remote URI.

Package: `Google_GenerativeAI`. Setup: [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization).

## Ways to Attach Media

| Method | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GeminiModel.GenerateContentAsync(prompt, filePath)` / `StreamContentAsync(prompt, filePath)` | Gemini API | Small files of a supported type are sent inline. Larger files (up to 2 GB) are uploaded with the Files API, and the call waits for them to become `ACTIVE`. |
| `request.AddInlineFile(filePath)` | Both | Reads the file and sends it inline as base64 (keep inline data under about 20 MB). |
| `request.AddInlineData(base64, mimeType)` | Both | You provide the base64 data yourself. |
| `request.AddRemoteFile(RemoteFile)` | Gemini API | A file uploaded with `FileClient`. See [Files Client](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Files-Client). |
| `request.AddRemoteFile(uri, mimeType)` | Both | A Files API URI, a `gs://` URI (Vertex AI) or a public URL. |

The file-path overloads are on `GeminiModel`. Create one with `GoogleAi.CreateGeminiModel(...)`.

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var googleAI = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY");
GeminiModel model = googleAI.CreateGeminiModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
```

## Identifying Objects in an Image (request builder)

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddInlineFile("image.png");
request.AddText("Identify objects in the image?");

var result = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
Console.WriteLine(result.Text());
```

## Image by File Path

```csharp
var result = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Identify objects in the image?", "image.png");
Console.WriteLine(result.Text());
```

## Video by File Path

```csharp
var result = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Describe this video?", "TestData/testvideo.mp4");
Console.WriteLine(result.Text());
```

Large videos are uploaded with the Files API first. `GeminiModel.TimeoutForFileStateCheck` (seconds, default 300) sets how long the call waits for the file to finish processing.

## Audio by File Path

```csharp
var result = await model.GenerateContentAsync("Describe this audio?", "TestData/testaudio.mp3");
Console.WriteLine(result.Text());
```

## Streaming with Multimodal Input

```csharp
await foreach (var chunk in model.StreamContentAsync("Identify objects in the image?", "image.png"))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Chunk: {chunk.Text()}");
}
```

## Chat with Multimodal Input and Streaming

`ChatSession` has no file-path overload. Add the file to a request instead:

```csharp
var chat = model.StartChat();

var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddInlineFile("image.png");
request.AddText("Identify objects in the image?");

await foreach (var chunk in chat.StreamContentAsync(request))
{
    Console.Write(chunk.Text());
}

var response2 = await chat.GenerateContentAsync("Can you estimate the number of blueberries?");
Console.WriteLine(response2.Text());
```

## Using an Uploaded File

```csharp
RemoteFile file = await model.Files!.UploadFileAsync("report.pdf");
await model.Files.AwaitForFileStateActiveAsync(file, 120, CancellationToken.None);

var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddRemoteFile(file);
request.AddText("Summarize this report.");

var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
```

## Vertex AI

On Vertex AI, models created with `VertexAI.CreateGenerativeModel` are plain `GenerativeModel` instances without the file-path overloads. Use inline data, or reference files in Cloud Storage:

```csharp
var vertex = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "global");
var vModel = vertex.CreateGenerativeModel(VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Flash);

var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddRemoteFile("gs://cloud-samples-data/generative-ai/audio/pixel.mp3", "audio/mp3");
request.AddText("What is this audio about?");

var response = await vModel.GenerateContentAsync(request);
```

## Media Resolution

`GenerationConfig.MediaResolution` (`MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW`, `MEDIA_RESOLUTION_MEDIUM` or `MEDIA_RESOLUTION_HIGH`) trades image and video detail against token cost:

```csharp
request.GenerationConfig = new GenerationConfig { MediaResolution = MediaResolution.MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW };
```

## Important Considerations

- **File paths**: Make sure the paths exist and your application can read them. Missing files throw `FileNotFoundException`.
- **Supported types**: The SDK checks MIME types against `InlineMimeTypes.AllowedMimeTypes` (inline) and `FilesConstants.SupportedMimeTypes` (upload). Unsupported types throw `NotSupportedException`.
- **Model capabilities**: Check that your model supports the input modality you send.
- **Streaming**: Chunks are partial. Join them if you need the complete output.

- [GeminiModel](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=GeminiModel)

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Json-Mode -->

JSON mode makes Gemini return structured JSON that matches a C# type. The SDK builds the response schema from your class, sends it with the request and deserializes the reply. It can also return enum values or pull JSON blocks out of free-form text.

Package: `Google_GenerativeAI`. Setup: [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization).

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var model = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY").CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);

public class SampleJsonClass
{
    public string? Name { get; set; }
    public int Age { get; set; }
}
```

## 1. Automatic JSON Handling

### `GenerateObjectAsync<T>`

Sets JSON mode with a schema built from `T`, sends the request and returns the deserialized object (or `null`).

#### With a text prompt

```csharp
var person = await model.GenerateObjectAsync<SampleJsonClass>("Give me a JSON object representing a person.");
if (person != null)
    Console.WriteLine($"Name: {person.Name}, Age: {person.Age}");
```

#### With a list of `Part` objects

Use parts to mix text with images or other media:

```csharp
var parts = new List<Part> { new Part { Text = "Give me a JSON object representing a person." } };
var person = await model.GenerateObjectAsync<SampleJsonClass>(parts);
```

#### With a full request

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddText("Give me a JSON object representing a person.");

var person = await model.GenerateObjectAsync<SampleJsonClass>(request);
```

To build the request from a `Content` object, add it with `request.AddContent(content)` and then call the request overload.

### `GenerateContentAsync<T>` and `ToObject<T>`

Use this form when you also need the full `GenerateContentResponse`, for example for usage metadata or finish reasons:

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddText("Give me a JSON object representing a person.");

GenerateContentResponse response = await model.GenerateContentAsync<SampleJsonClass>(request);
var person = response.ToObject<SampleJsonClass>();
```

### `UseJsonMode<T>` on the request

`UseJsonMode<T>()` sets `ResponseMimeType = "application/json"` and a `ResponseSchema` generated from `T`. Use it with the regular `GenerateContentAsync`:

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.UseJsonMode<SampleJsonClass>();
request.AddText("Give me a JSON object representing a person.");

var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
var person = response.ToObject<SampleJsonClass>();
```

### Lists of objects

For an array response, use `List<T>` as the type argument:

```csharp
List<SampleJsonClass>? people =
    await model.GenerateObjectAsync<List<SampleJsonClass>>("Give me three people as JSON.");
```

When a free-text response contains several separate JSON objects, `response.ToObjects<T>()` deserializes each block that matches `T` and returns them as a `List<T>`.

### Model-level JSON mode

Set `model.UseJsonMode = true` to make the model return JSON for every request. JSON mode can't be combined with Google Search, code execution or legacy grounding. Combining them throws `NotSupportedException`.

## 2. Enum Mode

`GenerateEnumAsync<T>` (or `request.UseEnumMode<T>()`) uses the `text/x.enum` MIME type, which limits the answer to one value of the enum:

```csharp
public enum Sentiment { Positive, Neutral, Negative }

var sentiment = await model.GenerateEnumAsync<Sentiment>("Classify: 'I love this product!'");
Console.WriteLine(sentiment);

// Or manually
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.UseEnumMode<Sentiment>();
request.AddText("Classify: 'The service was slow.'");
var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
var value = response.ToEnum<Sentiment>();
```

## 3. Manual Schema and JSON Parsing

### Setting the schema yourself

`GenerationConfig.ResponseSchema` takes a `Schema` (OpenAPI subset). `GoogleSchemaHelper.ConvertToSchema<T>()` builds one from a type. `ResponseJsonSchema` takes a raw JSON Schema as a `JsonNode`.

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.GenerationConfig = new GenerationConfig
{
    ResponseMimeType = "application/json",
    ResponseSchema = GoogleSchemaHelper.ConvertToSchema<SampleJsonClass>()
};
request.AddText("Give me a really good response.");
```

### Extracting JSON blocks from text

Without JSON mode, models often wrap JSON in Markdown code fences. `ExtractJsonBlocks()` finds those blocks, and `JsonBlock.ToObject<T>()` deserializes each one:

```csharp
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.AddText("Give me some JSON describing two people.");

var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
var jsonBlocks = response.ExtractJsonBlocks();
var myObjects = jsonBlocks.Select(block => block.ToObject<SampleJsonClass>());

foreach (var obj in myObjects)
{
    if (obj != null)
        Console.WriteLine($"Name: {obj.Name}, Age: {obj.Age}");
}
```

`ExtractJsonBlocks()` and `ToObject<T>()` are also available on `Content`, and `ExtractJsonBlocks()` on plain `string`.

## Serializer Options and NativeAOT

`model.GenerateObjectJsonSerializerOptions` controls how schemas are built and responses are deserialized. With NativeAOT or trimming, where reflection is disabled, pass options that include a source-generated `JsonSerializerContext` for your types:

```csharp
model.GenerateObjectJsonSerializerOptions = new JsonSerializerOptions
{
    TypeInfoResolver = MyJsonContext.Default
};

// Extension methods also accept options
var person = response.ToObject<SampleJsonClass>(MyJsonContext.Default.Options);
```

See [NativeAOT and Trimming Guidelines](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/NativeAOT-and-Trimming-Guidelines).

## Important Considerations

1. **Supported types**: The schema is built from public properties. Very dynamic types such as `Dictionary<,>` or `object` may not map well to a Gemini schema.
2. **Null results**: `ToObject<T>` and `GenerateObjectAsync<T>` return `null` when the response can't be deserialized. Check the result before you use it.
3. **Model compatibility**: Check that the model you use supports structured output (JSON mode and response schemas).

# Function Calling

Function calling lets Gemini call your own C# code to look up information or take actions. You describe your functions; the model decides when to call them; the SDK runs the call and sends the result back to the model, which then writes the final answer.

**NuGet packages**

```bash
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Tools
```

`Google_GenerativeAI.Tools` brings in the [CSharpToJsonSchema](https://www.nuget.org/packages/CSharpToJsonSchema) source generator, which provides the `[FunctionTool]` and `[GenerateJsonSchema]` attributes (namespace `CSharpToJsonSchema`).

## Ways to define tools

| Style | Main types | NativeAOT / trimming | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reflection-based | `QuickTool`, `QuickTools` | Needs a `JsonSerializerContext` (see [NativeAOT and Trimming Guidelines](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/NativeAOT-and-Trimming-Guidelines)) | Prototyping, lambdas, third-party methods |
| Method-based (source generated) | `[FunctionTool]` + generated `Tools` class | Fully compatible | A few static or instance methods |
| Interface-based (source generated) | `[GenerateJsonSchema]` + `GenericFunctionTool` | Fully compatible | Reusable tool sets with several methods |
| MCP servers | `McpTool` | See [MCP integration](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/MCP-(Model-Context-Protocol)-Integration) | Tools exposed by an external MCP server |

All of them end up as an `IFunctionTool` that you register with `GenerativeModel.AddFunctionTool(...)` (or `ChatSession.AddFunctionTool(...)`).

## 1. Reflection-based `QuickTool` and `QuickTools`

Wrap any delegate (lambda, static or instance method) at runtime.

```csharp
using System.ComponentModel;
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Tools;

var func = async ([Description("Request to query student record")] QueryStudentRecordRequest query) =>
{
    return new StudentRecord
    {
        StudentId = "12345",
        FullName = query.FullName,
        EnrolledCourses = new List<string> { "Math", "Physics", "Chemistry" },
        Grades = new Dictionary<string, double> { { "Math", 95.0 }, { "Physics", 89.0 }, { "Chemistry", 88.0 } },
        EnrollmentDate = new DateTime(2023, 1, 10),
        IsActive = true
    };
};

var quickTool = new QuickTool(func, "GetStudentRecordAsync", "Return student record for the year");
// For several delegates: new QuickTools(new Delegate[] { f1, f2, f3 })

var model = new GenerativeModel(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
model.AddFunctionTool(quickTool);

var result = await model.GenerateContentAsync(
    "How is John Joe doing in senior grade? Enrollment year 01-01-2024 to 01-01-2025");
Console.WriteLine(result.Text);

public class QueryStudentRecordRequest
{
    public string FullName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public DateTime EnrollmentYearFrom { get; set; }
    public DateTime EnrollmentYearTo { get; set; }
}

public class StudentRecord
{
    public string StudentId { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public string FullName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public List<string> EnrolledCourses { get; set; } = new();
    public Dictionary<string, double> Grades { get; set; } = new();
    public DateTime EnrollmentDate { get; set; }
    public bool IsActive { get; set; }
}
```

The `QuickTool` constructor is `QuickTool(Delegate func, string? name = null, string? description = null, JsonSerializerOptions? options = null)`. Pass `options` (or register a resolver in `DefaultSerializerOptions.CustomJsonTypeResolvers`) when you publish with NativeAOT or trimming.

For Microsoft.Extensions.AI, convert with `quickTool.AsMeaiTool()` or `quickTools.ToMeaiFunctions()`.

## 2. Method-based tools with `[FunctionTool]`

Mark methods with `[FunctionTool]`. The source generator creates a `Tools` class that wraps them, with no reflection at runtime.

```csharp
using System.ComponentModel;
using CSharpToJsonSchema;
using GenerativeAI;

public static class BookTools
{
    [FunctionTool(GoogleFunctionTool = true, MeaiFunctionTool = true)]
    [Description("Get book page content")]
    public static Task<string> GetBookPageContentAsync(string bookName, int bookPageNumber,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        return Task.FromResult("There is nice weather outside, and I am stuck at home.");
    }
}

// Gemini (GoogleFunctionTool = true)
var model = new GenerativeModel(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
var tools = new Tools([BookTools.GetBookPageContentAsync]);
model.AddFunctionTool(tools);

// Microsoft.Extensions.AI (MeaiFunctionTool = true)
chatOptions.Tools = tools.AsMeaiTools();
```

- `GoogleFunctionTool = true` makes the generated `Tools` usable with `AddFunctionTool`.
- `MeaiFunctionTool = true` generates `AsMeaiTools()` for use with `ChatOptions.Tools` (see [Microsoft.Extensions.AI](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Microsoft.Extensions.AI-IChatClient-Implementation)).

## 3. Interface-based tools with `[GenerateJsonSchema]`

### Define the interface

Put `[GenerateJsonSchema]` on an interface. Add `[Description]` attributes to methods and parameters so the model knows what they do.

```csharp
using System.ComponentModel;
using CSharpToJsonSchema;

[GenerateJsonSchema(GoogleFunctionTool = true, MeaiFunctionTool = true)]
public interface IWeatherFunctions
{
    [Description("Get the current weather in a given location")]
    Weather GetCurrentWeather(
        [Description("The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA")] string location,
        Unit unit = Unit.Celsius);

    [Description("Get the current weather in a given location asynchronously")]
    Task<Weather> GetCurrentWeatherAsync(
        [Description("The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA")] string location,
        Unit unit = Unit.Celsius,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}

public enum Unit { Celsius, Fahrenheit, Imperial }

public class Weather
{
    public string Location { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public double Temperature { get; set; }
    public Unit Unit { get; set; }
    public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
}
```

Both `GoogleFunctionTool` and `MeaiFunctionTool` are optional (default `false`):

- `GoogleFunctionTool = true` generates `AsGoogleFunctionTool()`.
- `MeaiFunctionTool = true` generates `AsMeaiTools()`.

### Implement the interface

```csharp
public class WeatherService : IWeatherFunctions
{
    public Weather GetCurrentWeather(string location, Unit unit = Unit.Celsius) =>
        new() { Location = location, Temperature = 30.0, Unit = unit, Description = "Sunny" };

    public Task<Weather> GetCurrentWeatherAsync(string location, Unit unit = Unit.Celsius,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) =>
        Task.FromResult(new Weather { Location = location, Temperature = 22.0, Unit = unit, Description = "Sunny" });
}
```

Replace the placeholder values with your real logic.

### Register the tools

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Tools;

var service = new WeatherService();
var model = new GenerativeModel(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);

// With GoogleFunctionTool = true:
model.AddFunctionTool(service.AsGoogleFunctionTool());

// Always available (works without GoogleFunctionTool = true):
model.AddFunctionTool(new GenericFunctionTool(service.AsTools(), service.AsCalls()));

// Microsoft.Extensions.AI, with MeaiFunctionTool = true:
chatOptions.Tools = service.AsMeaiTools();
```

## Making a request

```csharp
var result = await model.GenerateContentAsync("What is the weather in San Francisco today?");
Console.WriteLine(result.Text);
```

The model reads your descriptions and decides whether to call a function. With the default settings the SDK runs the function, sends the result back, and returns the model's final answer.

Tools also work in a multi-turn chat:

```csharp
var chat = model.StartChat();
chat.AddFunctionTool(service.AsGoogleFunctionTool());
var reply = await chat.GenerateContentAsync("Is it warmer in Paris or in Rome?");
```

## Function calling behaviour

Use `GenerativeModel.FunctionCallingBehaviour` (type `GenerativeAI.Core.FunctionCallingBehaviour`) to control the automatic loop:

```csharp
model.FunctionCallingBehaviour = new FunctionCallingBehaviour
{
    FunctionEnabled = true,            // send the tools to the model (default true)
    AutoCallFunction = true,           // run requested functions automatically (default true)
    AutoReplyFunction = true,          // send results back and return the model's final answer (default true)
    AutoHandleBadFunctionCalls = false // try to recover from invalid function calls (default false)
};
```

| Property | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FunctionEnabled` | `true` | Turns function calling on or off. `model.DisableFunctions()` and `model.EnableFunctions()` are shortcuts. |
| `AutoCallFunction` | `true` | If `true`, the SDK runs the function the model asks for. If `false`, the function call is returned in the response for you to handle. |
| `AutoReplyFunction` | `true` | If `true`, the function result is sent back to the model and you get its final answer. If `false`, the function runs but the SDK returns the model's function-call response instead of sending the result back. |
| `AutoHandleBadFunctionCalls` | `false` | If the model calls a function that no registered tool contains: `false` throws a `GenerativeAIException`; `true` sends an error result (`"Invalid function name or function doesn't exist."`) back to the model instead. |

When the model asks for several functions in one turn (parallel function calling), the SDK runs all of them and returns all results in a single turn.

You can also pass a `ToolConfig` and a behaviour per tool: `model.AddFunctionTool(tool, toolConfig, functionCallingBehaviour)`. For example, to force the model to call one of your functions:

```csharp
model.AddFunctionTool(tool, new ToolConfig
{
    FunctionCallingConfig = new FunctionCallingConfig
    {
        Mode = FunctionCallingMode.ANY, // AUTO, ANY, NONE or VALIDATED
        AllowedFunctionNames = new List<string> { "GetCurrentWeather" }
    }
});
```

## Handling function calls manually

Set `AutoCallFunction = false` to get the function call back and run it yourself. Send the result back as a `FunctionResponse` part in a turn with the **`user`** role:

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

model.FunctionCallingBehaviour.AutoCallFunction = false;

var userTurn = new Content { Role = Roles.User };
userTurn.AddText("What's the weather in San Francisco?");

var request = new GenerateContentRequest { Contents = new List<Content> { userTurn } };
var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);

var call = response.GetFunction(); // or response.GetFunctions() for parallel calls
if (call != null)
{
    FunctionResponse? result = await tool.CallAsync(call); // any IFunctionTool, e.g. the GenericFunctionTool above

    request.Contents.Add(response.Candidates![0].Content!);   // the model's function-call turn
    var resultTurn = new Content { Role = Roles.User };         // Gemini 3.x rejects the "function" role
    resultTurn.AddPart(new Part { FunctionResponse = result });
    request.Contents.Add(resultTurn);

    var final = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
    Console.WriteLine(final.Text);
}
```

### v4 change: function results use the `user` role

Since v4.0.0 the SDK sends function results in a `user` turn, as the official SDKs do, because Gemini 3.x models reject the legacy `function` role. Before each request, `GenerativeModel` converts any content with `Role == Roles.Function` to `Roles.User`, so chat histories saved by earlier SDK versions keep working without changes.

## Choosing a style

**Interface-based (`[GenerateJsonSchema]`) and method-based (`[FunctionTool]`) tools**

- Fully compatible with NativeAOT and trimming, because the schema and the call code are generated at compile time.
- Interface-based tools suit reusable tool sets with several methods: define the set once and reuse it across your solution. Use cases: plugin systems, microservice communication, domain-specific languages, data access layers, workflow automation, AI-driven data validation (validation rules defined as an interface), personalised learning platforms (one interface per learning module).
- Method-based tools suit a small number of class-scoped or static methods. Use cases: command-line integration, configuration management, hardware control, simple utility functions, real-time data analysis (wrapping single analysis methods), context-aware notifications.

**Reflection-based `QuickTool` and `QuickTools`**

- Not recommended when NativeAOT or trimming matters (or provide a `JsonSerializerContext`, see [NativeAOT and Trimming Guidelines](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/NativeAOT-and-Trimming-Guidelines)).
- Useful for calling functions from third-party libraries whose source you don't control, and for anonymous functions while testing prompts or prototyping.
- Use cases: dynamic scripting, rapid prototyping of API integrations, debugging and testing, event handling, data transformation pipelines, AI-powered data scraping, quickly creating input-validation tools, A/B testing of function logic.

**In summary**

- For performance and NativeAOT/trimming compatibility, use interface-based tools or method-based tools with `[FunctionTool]`.
- For rapid prototyping, testing or third-party libraries, use `QuickTool` and `QuickTools`.
- Use interface-based tools for reusable tool sets and method-based tools for a few methods.

---

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Embeddings -->

Embeddings are vectors of numbers that capture the meaning of text (and, for some models, other media). Use them for semantic search, similarity, clustering, classification and retrieval-augmented generation. In this SDK you create an `EmbeddingModel` and call `EmbedContentAsync` or `BatchEmbedContentAsync`. The same API works on the Gemini Developer API and on Vertex AI.

Package: `Google_GenerativeAI`. For `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` `IEmbeddingGenerator` support, see [Microsoft.Extensions.AI](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Microsoft.Extensions.AI-IChatClient-Implementation).

## Supported Models

| Platform | Constant | Model | How the SDK calls it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini API | `GoogleAIModels.GeminiEmbedding2` | `models/gemini-embedding-2` | `embedContent` / `batchEmbedContents` |
| Gemini API | `GoogleAIModels.GeminiEmbedding` | `models/gemini-embedding-001` | `embedContent` / `batchEmbedContents` |
| Vertex AI | `VertexAIModels.Embeddings.GeminiEmbedding001` | `gemini-embedding-001` | `embedContent` (Vertex format) |
| Vertex AI | `VertexAIModels.Gemini.TextEmbedding005` | `text-embedding-005` | `predict` |
| Vertex AI | `VertexAIModels.Embeddings.TextMultilingualEmbedding002`, `MultimodalEmbedding`, ... | others | `predict` |

The SDK validates the model name against `SupportedEmbedingModels.All` and throws `NotSupportedException` for models that aren't listed. On Vertex AI, model names containing `gemini` (and `maas` models) use `embedContent`. All other models use `predict`. The response always comes back as the same `EmbedContentResponse` / `BatchEmbedContentsResponse` types.

> **Vertex AI location:** `gemini-embedding-001` and `text-embedding-005` aren't served from the `global` endpoint. Create a separate `VertexAI` instance with a regional location such as `us-central1` for embeddings (see [Initialization](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Initialization#choosing-a-region-global-vs-regional)).

## Creating an Embedding Model

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

// Gemini API
var googleAI = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY");
var embeddingModel = googleAI.CreateEmbeddingModel(GoogleAIModels.GeminiEmbedding);

// Vertex AI (regional location)
var vertexAI = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "us-central1");
var vertexEmbeddingModel = vertexAI.CreateEmbeddingModel(VertexAIModels.Embeddings.GeminiEmbedding001);

// Or directly
var model2 = new EmbeddingModel("YOUR_API_KEY", GoogleAIModels.GeminiEmbedding2);
```

## Generating Embeddings

Every method accepts an optional `CancellationToken`.

### `EmbedContentAsync(string message)`

```csharp
EmbedContentResponse response = await embeddingModel.EmbedContentAsync("This is a test embedding.");
List<float>? vector = response.Embedding?.Values;
```

### `EmbedContentAsync(Content content)`

```csharp
var content = new Content("This is a test embedding.", Roles.User);
EmbedContentResponse response = await embeddingModel.EmbedContentAsync(content);
```

### `EmbedContentAsync(EmbedContentRequest request)`

Use a request to set the task type, title and output size:

```csharp
var request = new EmbedContentRequest
{
    Content = new Content("Paris is the capital of France.", Roles.User),
    TaskType = TaskType.RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT,
    Title = "Geography facts",          // only allowed with RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT
    OutputDimensionality = 256          // truncate the vector to 256 dimensions
};

EmbedContentResponse response = await embeddingModel.EmbedContentAsync(request);
Console.WriteLine(response.Embedding?.Values?.Count); // 256
```

### `EmbedContentAsync(IEnumerable<Part> parts)`

```csharp
var parts = new List<Part> { new Part { Text = "This is a test embedding." } };
EmbedContentResponse response = await embeddingModel.EmbedContentAsync(parts);
```

### `EmbedContentAsync(IEnumerable<string> messages)`

> **Note:** This overload joins all strings into **one** content and returns **one** embedding. To get one embedding per string, use `BatchEmbedContentAsync`.

```csharp
var messages = new List<string> { "This is a test embedding.", "Another test embedding." };
EmbedContentResponse response = await embeddingModel.EmbedContentAsync(messages); // single embedding
```

### `BatchEmbedContentAsync(IEnumerable<EmbedContentRequest> requests)`

Returns one embedding per request, in order. This is the most efficient way to embed many inputs:

```csharp
var requests = new List<EmbedContentRequest>
{
    new EmbedContentRequest { Content = new Content("This is a test embedding.", Roles.User), TaskType = TaskType.RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT },
    new EmbedContentRequest { Content = new Content("Another test embedding.", Roles.User),  TaskType = TaskType.RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT }
};

BatchEmbedContentsResponse response = await embeddingModel.BatchEmbedContentAsync(requests);
foreach (var embedding in response.Embeddings ?? new List<ContentEmbedding>())
{
    Console.WriteLine(embedding.Values?.Count);
}
```

### `BatchEmbedContentAsync(IEnumerable<Content> contents)`

```csharp
var contents = new List<Content>
{
    new Content("This is a test embedding.", Roles.User),
    new Content("Another test embedding.", Roles.User)
};

BatchEmbedContentsResponse response = await embeddingModel.BatchEmbedContentAsync(contents);
```

## Task Types

`TaskType` tells the model what the embedding will be used for, which improves quality for that use:

| Value | Use for |
|---|---|
| `RETRIEVAL_QUERY` | Search queries |
| `RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT` | Documents being indexed (the only type that allows `Title`) |
| `SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY` | Comparing text similarity |
| `CLASSIFICATION` | Text classification |
| `CLUSTERING` | Clustering |
| `CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY` | Code search queries |
| `QUESTION_ANSWERING` | Questions in a QA system |
| `FACT_VERIFICATION` | Statements to verify |

## Vertex AI-Only Options

These `EmbedContentRequest` properties are only sent on Vertex AI. On the Gemini API they throw `NotSupportedException`.

| Property | Description |
|---|---|
| `AutoTruncate` | Truncate input that is longer than the model's limit instead of failing |
| `DocumentOcr` | Run OCR on document input (Gemini embedding models only) |
| `AudioTrackExtraction` | Extract the audio track from video input (Gemini embedding models only) |
| `MimeType` | MIME type of the input (`predict` models) |

```csharp
var vertexAI = new VertexAI("your-project-id", "us-central1");
var textEmbedding = vertexAI.CreateEmbeddingModel(VertexAIModels.Gemini.TextEmbedding005);

var response = await textEmbedding.EmbedContentAsync(new EmbedContentRequest
{
    Content = new Content("What is the capital of France?", Roles.User),
    TaskType = TaskType.RETRIEVAL_QUERY,
    OutputDimensionality = 128,
    AutoTruncate = true
});

var stats = response.Embedding?.Statistics; // TokenCount, Truncated
```

Rules for Vertex `predict` models (such as `text-embedding-005`): in a batch, every request must use the same `OutputDimensionality` and `AutoTruncate`. `DocumentOcr` and `AudioTrackExtraction` aren't allowed. Vertex `maas` embedding models accept only one content per batch request.

## Response Types

- `EmbedContentResponse.Embedding` is a `ContentEmbedding` with `Values` (`List<float>`) and optional `Statistics` (`TokenCount`, `Truncated`, `TokensDetails`).
- `BatchEmbedContentsResponse.Embeddings` is a `List<ContentEmbedding>`, one per input.

## Errors

API errors throw `GenerativeAI.Exceptions.ApiException`. If you use a model the region doesn't serve, the API returns an error. Switch to a regional location.

- [Microsoft.Extensions.AI](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Microsoft.Extensions.AI-IChatClient-Implementation)

- [EmbedContentRequest](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=EmbedContentRequest)
- [EmbedContentResponse](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=EmbedContentResponse)
- [BatchEmbedContentRequest](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=BatchEmbedContentRequest)
- [BatchEmbedContentsResponse](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=BatchEmbedContentsResponse)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Context-Caching -->

Context caching stores a large context once and reuses it across many requests. The context can be documents, files, conversation history or a system instruction. Cached tokens are billed at a lower rate than regular input tokens, and responses can come back faster. In this SDK, `CachingClient` creates and manages caches, and `GenerativeModel.CachedContent` attaches a cache to a model.

Package: `Google_GenerativeAI`. Namespaces: `GenerativeAI.Clients` (`CachingClient`) and `GenerativeAI.Types` (`CachedContent`, `Duration`).

> This page documents caching on the **Gemini Developer API**, which is the platform covered by the SDK's caching tests.

## Getting a `CachingClient`

Every `GenerativeModel` has a ready-made `CachingClient` property. You can also create a client from a platform adapter:

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Clients;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var googleAi = new GoogleAi("YOUR_API_KEY");
var model = googleAi.CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
CachingClient cachingClient = model.CachingClient!;

// Or standalone
var platform = new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter("YOUR_API_KEY");
var cachingClient2 = new CachingClient(platform);
```

## Methods

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `CreateCachedContentAsync(CachedContent)` | Creates a cache from contents, a system instruction, tools and a TTL or expiry |
| `GetCachedContentAsync(name)` | Gets a cache by name (`cachedContents/{id}` or just `{id}`) |
| `ListCachedContentsAsync(pageSize, pageToken)` | Lists caches, one page at a time |
| `UpdateCachedContentAsync(cacheName, cachedContent, updateMask)` | Updates `ttl` or `expireTime` (PATCH) |
| `DeleteCachedContentAsync(name)` | Deletes a cache |

All methods accept a `CancellationToken`.

## `CachedContent` Properties

| Property | Notes |
|---|---|
| `Model` | **Required.** Must match the model you'll use, for example `GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash` (`models/gemini-3.8-flash`) |
| `Contents` | The content to cache (`List<Content>`) |
| `SystemInstruction` | Optional `Content` |
| `Tools`, `ToolConfig` | Optional tools stored with the cache |
| `Ttl` | `Duration`, for example `new Duration { Seconds = 3600 }`, or `TimeSpan.FromHours(1)` through the implicit conversion |
| `ExpireTime` | `Timestamp`. Use it instead of `Ttl`. Converts implicitly from `DateTime` |
| `DisplayName` | Optional friendly name |
| `KmsKeyName` | Customer-managed encryption key (a Vertex AI field) |
| `Name`, `CreateTime`, `UpdateTime`, `UsageMetadata` | Output only |

## 1. Creating Cached Content

```csharp
var longDocument = await File.ReadAllTextAsync("path/to/long-document.txt");

var cachedContent = new CachedContent
{
    DisplayName = "Product Documentation Cache",
    Model = GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash, // must match the model you'll use later
    Contents = new List<Content>
    {
        new Content(longDocument, Roles.User)
    },
    Ttl = new Duration { Seconds = 3600 } // expires after 1 hour
};

CachedContent createdCache = await cachingClient.CreateCachedContentAsync(cachedContent);
Console.WriteLine($"Cache created: {createdCache.Name}");
Console.WriteLine($"Expires at: {createdCache.ExpireTime}");
Console.WriteLine($"Token count: {createdCache.UsageMetadata?.TotalTokenCount}");
```

### With a system instruction

```csharp
var cache = await cachingClient.CreateCachedContentAsync(new CachedContent
{
    DisplayName = "Customer Support Bot Cache",
    Model = GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash,
    SystemInstruction = new Content("You are a helpful customer support agent. Be professional and concise.", null),
    Contents = new List<Content>
    {
        new Content("Company policies and FAQs:\n\n[Large document content here]", Roles.User)
    },
    Ttl = TimeSpan.FromHours(2)
});
```

### With multiple documents

```csharp
var multiCache = await cachingClient.CreateCachedContentAsync(new CachedContent
{
    DisplayName = "Multi-Document Cache",
    Model = GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash,
    Contents = new List<Content>
    {
        new Content("Document 1: Product Specifications\n\n" + doc1, Roles.User),
        new Content("I've processed the product specifications.", Roles.Model),
        new Content("Document 2: User Manual\n\n" + doc2, Roles.User)
    },
    Ttl = new Duration { Seconds = 7200 }
});
```

Uploaded files can be cached as well. Add parts that reference a `RemoteFile` from [Files Client](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Files-Client).

## 2. Using Cached Content with `GenerativeModel`

Set the model's `CachedContent` property. Every request then sends the cache name.

```csharp
var model = new GenerativeModel(platform, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash)
{
    CachedContent = createdCache
};

var response1 = await model.GenerateContentAsync("What are the main features of this product?");
Console.WriteLine(response1.Text());

// Reuses the same cached context
var response2 = await model.GenerateContentAsync("What is the pricing structure?");
Console.WriteLine(response2.Text());

Console.WriteLine($"Cached tokens used: {response2.UsageMetadata?.CachedContentTokenCount}");
```

You can also attach an existing cache to a model you already have:

```csharp
CachedContent? retrieved = await cachingClient.GetCachedContentAsync("cachedContents/your-cache-id");
model.CachedContent = retrieved;
```

When `CachedContent` is set, the SDK:

- throws `ArgumentException` if `model.Model` is not exactly equal to `CachedContent.Model`;
- removes `Tools`, `ToolConfig` and `SystemInstruction` from the request, because they must be part of the cache instead;
- throws `NotSupportedException` if Google Search, code execution or legacy grounding is enabled on the model.

To set the cache per request instead, set `GenerateContentRequest.CachedContent` to the cache name.

## 3. Listing and Getting Caches

```csharp
var cachedList = await cachingClient.ListCachedContentsAsync(pageSize: 10);

foreach (var item in cachedList.CachedContents ?? new List<CachedContent>())
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{item.Name} | {item.DisplayName} | {item.Model} | created {item.CreateTime} | expires {item.ExpireTime}");
}

if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(cachedList.NextPageToken))
{
    var nextPage = await cachingClient.ListCachedContentsAsync(10, cachedList.NextPageToken);
}

var specificCache = await cachingClient.GetCachedContentAsync("cachedContents/your-cache-id");
Console.WriteLine($"Retrieved cache: {specificCache?.DisplayName}");
```

## 4. Updating a Cache (extend TTL)

Only `ttl` and `expireTime` can change after a cache is created. Use `updateMask` to name the field you're changing.

```csharp
var updatedCache = await cachingClient.UpdateCachedContentAsync(
    cacheName: createdCache.Name!,
    cachedContent: new CachedContent { Ttl = new Duration { Seconds = 7200 } },
    updateMask: "ttl");

Console.WriteLine($"New expiration: {updatedCache?.ExpireTime}");

// Or set an absolute expiry
await cachingClient.UpdateCachedContentAsync(createdCache.Name!,
    new CachedContent { ExpireTime = DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(4) }, "expireTime");
```

## 5. Deleting a Cache

```csharp
await cachingClient.DeleteCachedContentAsync(createdCache.Name!);
```

## Complete Example

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Clients;
using GenerativeAI.Exceptions;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var apiKey = System.Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GOOGLE_API_KEY"); // "System." avoids a clash with GenerativeAI.Types.Environment
var platform = new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey);
var cachingClient = new CachingClient(platform);

using var httpClient = new HttpClient();
var largeContext = await httpClient.GetStringAsync(
    "https://storage.googleapis.com/generativeai-downloads/data/a11.txt");

var cache = await cachingClient.CreateCachedContentAsync(new CachedContent
{
    DisplayName = "Apollo 11 transcript",
    Model = GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash,
    SystemInstruction = new Content("You are an expert on the Apollo program.", null),
    Contents = new List<Content> { new Content($"Transcript:\n\n{largeContext}", Roles.User) },
    Ttl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30)
});
Console.WriteLine($"Cache created: {cache.Name}, tokens: {cache.UsageMetadata?.TotalTokenCount}");

try
{
    var model = new GenerativeModel(platform, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash) { CachedContent = cache };

    foreach (var question in new[]
             {
                 "Summarize the main events.",
                 "What problems did the crew report?",
                 "Describe the landing sequence."
             })
    {
        var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(question);
        Console.WriteLine($"\nQ: {question}\nA: {response.Text()}");
    }
}
finally
{
    await cachingClient.DeleteCachedContentAsync(cache.Name!);
}
```

## Error Handling

API errors throw `ApiException`. For example, you can retry once when rate limited:

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Exceptions;

async Task<CachedContent?> CreateCacheWithRetry(CachingClient client, CachedContent content)
{
    try
    {
        return await client.CreateCachedContentAsync(content);
    }
    catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.ErrorCode == 429)
    {
        await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
        return await client.CreateCachedContentAsync(content);
    }
    catch (ApiException ex)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Failed to create cache: {ex.ErrorCode} {ex.ErrorStatus} {ex.ErrorMessage}");
        return null;
    }
}
```

Getting or deleting a cache that doesn't exist also throws.

## Key Benefits

1. **Cost savings**: Cached tokens are billed at a lower rate than regular input tokens.
2. **Performance**: The cached context isn't processed again on every request.
3. **Consistency**: Every request uses the same context.
4. **Large context**: You can cache content up to the model's context window.

## Considerations

- **Model matching**: `CachedContent.Model` must equal `GenerativeModel.Model` exactly. Use the same constant for both.
- **Tool restrictions**: You can't combine Google Search, code execution or grounding with a cache on the model. Tools, tool config and system instructions belong in the cache.
- **Immutability**: Content, system instruction, tools and model can't change after creation. Only `ttl` and `expireTime` can.
- **TTL management**: Caches expire automatically. Extend them with `UpdateCachedContentAsync`.
- **Minimum size**: Each model has a minimum number of tokens it will cache, and it differs between models. Check the [Gemini caching docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching) for current limits.
- **Cost structure**: Creating and storing a cache costs money (storage is billed per token-hour). Delete caches you no longer need.
- **Resource names**: You can pass names as `cachedContents/{id}` or `{id}`.

## When to Use It

**Good fit:** analysing large documents with many questions, RAG with a fixed corpus, multi-turn conversations over the same material, code-repository analysis, support bots with large knowledge bases, educational, legal or medical document Q&A.

**Not a good fit:** one-off queries, context that changes often, small contexts below the model's minimum, and very short sessions where the cost of creating the cache isn't recovered.

## Cost Optimization Tips

1. Ask as many questions per cache as you can, to spread the creation cost.
2. Choose a TTL that matches how long you'll actually use the cache.
3. Reuse caches for recurring workloads instead of creating new ones.
4. Delete caches when you're done.

- [GetCachedContentAsync](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=GetCachedContentAsync)
- [UpdateCachedContentAsync](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=UpdateCachedContentAsync)
- [DeleteCachedContentAsync](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=DeleteCachedContentAsync)

# Interactions API

The Interactions API (`/interactions`) is a stateful API for model and agent interactions. Each call creates an
`Interaction` that the server can store, stream, run in the background and continue later. It is also the way to
call agents such as Deep Research and Antigravity.

The SDK exposes it through `InteractionsClient` (namespace `GenerativeAI.Clients`). It follows python-genai's
`client.interactions`, including stream reconnection and automatic continuation of long outputs.

| Platform | Support |
|---|---|
| Gemini API | Yes |
| Vertex AI | The client builds the Vertex URL (`.../projects/{project}/locations/{location}/interactions`). Whether a model is available there depends on the project and region. |

## Prerequisites

- NuGet package: `Google_GenerativeAI`
- A Gemini API key (`GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY`) or Vertex AI credentials. See [Authentication](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication).

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Clients;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

// Either use a factory method...
var googleAi = new GoogleAi(apiKey);
InteractionsClient client = googleAi.CreateInteractionsClient();

// ...or construct it directly from a platform adapter.
var client2 = new InteractionsClient(new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey));
```

Model IDs for the Interactions API are in `InteractionModels` (for example `InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash`).
Agent IDs are in `InteractionAgents` (for example `InteractionAgents.DeepResearchPreview042026`).

## Create an interaction

```csharp
var interaction = await client.CreateAsync(InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash, "Explain RAG in two sentences.");

Console.WriteLine(interaction.Id);      // keep it to fetch, continue or delete later
Console.WriteLine(interaction.Status);  // e.g. InteractionStatuses.Completed
Console.WriteLine(interaction.OutputText);
```

For more options, use `CreateInteractionRequest`:

```csharp
var request = new CreateInteractionRequest
{
    Model = InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash,
    Input = "Write a haiku about the ocean.",          // string converts to InteractionInput implicitly
    SystemInstruction = "You are a concise poet.",
    GenerationConfig = new InteractionGenerationConfig
    {
        MaxOutputTokens = 512,
        Temperature = 0.7,
        ThinkingLevel = InteractionThinkingLevels.Low
    },
    Tools = new List<InteractionTool> { new InteractionGoogleSearchTool() }
};

var result = await client.CreateAsync(request);
Console.WriteLine(result.OutputText);
```

Useful properties of `Interaction`: `Id`, `Status`, `Steps`, `Usage` (`InteractionUsage`), `OutputText`,
`OutputImage`, `OutputAudio`, `OutputVideo`, `FunctionCalls`, `ContinuationToken` and `Errors`.

Request rules (checked by the client before sending; an `ArgumentException` is thrown otherwise):

- Set exactly one of `Model` or `Agent`.
- `GenerationConfig` and `CachedContent` cannot be used with `Agent`.
- `AgentConfig` cannot be used with `Model`.

### Multi-turn conversations

The server stores interactions by default (`Store` is `null`/`true`). To continue a conversation, reference the
previous interaction:

```csharp
var first = await client.CreateAsync(InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash, "My name is Ada.");
var second = await client.CreateAsync(new CreateInteractionRequest
{
    Model = InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash,
    Input = "What is my name?",
    PreviousInteractionId = first.Id
});
```

## Thinking levels

`InteractionGenerationConfig.ThinkingLevel` takes a value from `InteractionThinkingLevels`:
`Minimal`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `XHigh`.

Not every model accepts every level. For example, **`gemini-3.8-flash` (`InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash`) accepts
`low`, `medium` and `high`, but not `minimal`**. The server rejects an unsupported level with a 400 error.
Use `Low` when you want cheap, fast requests.

## Streaming

`StreamAsync` sends `stream=true` and yields Server-Sent Events as typed `InteractionSseEvent` objects:

```csharp
var request = new CreateInteractionRequest
{
    Model = InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash,
    Input = "Tell me a short story.",
    GenerationConfig = new InteractionGenerationConfig { ThinkingLevel = InteractionThinkingLevels.Low }
};

await foreach (var e in client.StreamAsync(request))
{
    switch (e)
    {
        case InteractionCreatedEvent created:
            Console.WriteLine($"Interaction {created.Interaction?.Id} created");
            break;
        case InteractionStepDeltaEvent { Delta: InteractionTextDelta delta }:
            Console.Write(delta.Text);
            break;
        case InteractionStatusUpdateEvent status:
            Console.WriteLine($"\nStatus: {status.Status}");
            break;
        case InteractionCompletedEvent completed:
            Console.WriteLine($"\nDone: {completed.Interaction?.Status}");
            break;
        case InteractionErrorEvent error:
            Console.WriteLine($"Error: {error.Error?.Message}");
            break;
    }
}
```

Event types: `InteractionCreatedEvent`, `InteractionStepStartEvent`, `InteractionStepDeltaEvent`,
`InteractionStepStopEvent`, `InteractionStatusUpdateEvent`, `InteractionCompletedEvent`, `InteractionErrorEvent`
and `UnknownInteractionSseEvent`. Delta types include `InteractionTextDelta`, `InteractionThoughtSummaryDelta`,
`InteractionArgumentsDelta`, `InteractionImageDelta`, `InteractionAudioDelta` and others.

**Stream reconnection.** If the connection drops after the interaction was created, `StreamAsync` resumes from the
last received event ID automatically, up to `MaxStreamReconnects` times (default 3; set 0 to disable). You can also
resume a stream yourself, or stream an existing (for example background) interaction:

```csharp
await foreach (var e in client.ResumeStreamAsync(interactionId, lastEventId: lastSeenEventId))
{
    // ...
}
```

## Background mode

Set `Background = true` to queue the interaction and return immediately. Then poll it with
`WaitForCompletionAsync`, which returns once the status is no longer `in_progress` or `queued`:

```csharp
var created = await client.CreateAsync(new CreateInteractionRequest
{
    Model = InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash,
    Input = "Summarize the history of the printing press.",
    Background = true
});

var final = await client.WaitForCompletionAsync(
    created.Id!,
    pollInterval: TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5),   // default 10 s
    timeout: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10));      // throws TimeoutException when exceeded

if (final.Status == InteractionStatuses.Completed)
    Console.WriteLine(final.OutputText);
```

Agents normally run in the background:

```csharp
var research = await client.CreateAsync(new CreateInteractionRequest
{
    Agent = InteractionAgents.DeepResearchPreview042026,
    Input = "Compare recent approaches to battery recycling.",
    Background = true
});
var report = await client.WaitForCompletionAsync(research.Id!, timeout: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30));
```

Cancel a running background interaction with `CancelAsync(id)`.

Instead of polling, you can also receive a webhook when an interaction finishes: set
`CreateInteractionRequest.WebhookConfig` (`InteractionWebhookConfig` with `Uris` and `UserMetadata`) or register a
webhook for `WebhookEvents.InteractionCompleted`. See [Webhooks](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Webhooks).

## Get and delete

```csharp
var fetched = await client.GetAsync(interactionId, includeInput: true);
await client.DeleteAsync(interactionId);
```

IDs with an `interactions/` prefix are accepted.

## Automatic continuation

Very long outputs can end with status `InteractionStatuses.RequiresContinuation` and a `ContinuationToken`.
Like python-genai, `CreateAsync` continues such interactions for you:

- `EnableAutomaticContinuation` (default `true`): resume while the server asks for it. The returned interaction
  is the last hop, and its `Steps` contain the steps of all hops.
- `MaxContinuations` (default 10): the maximum number of extra requests per `CreateAsync` call.
- Background interactions are not continued by the client; the server continues them.

To control it yourself, turn it off and use `ContinueAsync` (or build the request with the static
`InteractionsClient.CreateContinuationRequest`):

```csharp
client.EnableAutomaticContinuation = false;

var interaction = await client.CreateAsync(request);
while (interaction.Status == InteractionStatuses.RequiresContinuation)
{
    interaction = await client.ContinueAsync(interaction, request);
}
```

Each continuation re-processes and bills input tokens.

## Error handling

HTTP errors are thrown as `GenerativeAI.Exceptions.ApiException`, with `ErrorCode`, `ErrorStatus` and
`ErrorMessage`:

```csharp
try
{
    var interaction = await client.CreateAsync(request);
}
catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.ErrorCode == 400)
{
    // For example an unsupported thinking level, or a model/agent that rejects background=true.
    Console.WriteLine($"{ex.ErrorStatus}: {ex.ErrorMessage}");
}
catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.ErrorCode is 429)
{
    // Quota exhausted: retry later.
}
```

Also check `interaction.Status` (`Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Incomplete`, `BudgetExceeded`, `RequiresAction`) and
`interaction.Errors`. `WaitForCompletionAsync` throws `TimeoutException` when its timeout is exceeded.

## Related pages

- [Webhooks](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Webhooks): get notified when an interaction completes
- [Agent APIs](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Agent-APIs): agents, environments, triggers and credentials used by agent interactions
- [File Search](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/File-Search): `InteractionFileSearchTool`
- [Generate Content](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Generate-Content) and [Streaming](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Streaming): the classic `generateContent` API

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Live-API -->

# Multimodal Live API

The Live API is a low-latency, bidirectional WebSocket API for real-time voice and video conversations with Gemini.
The SDK implements it in a separate package, **`Google_GenerativeAI.Live`**, with two clients:

- `MultiModalLiveClient`: Live sessions with Gemini Live models (text, audio and video in; audio out).
- `LiveMusicClient`: real-time music generation with Lyria RealTime ([Live Music](#live-music-lyria-realtime)).

Both are in the `GenerativeAI.Live` namespace.

| Feature | Gemini API | Vertex AI |
|---|---|---|
| `MultiModalLiveClient` | Yes | Yes (via `VertextPlatformAdapter`) |
| `SendAudioStreamEndAsync` | Yes | No (Gemini API only) |
| Ephemeral auth tokens (`AuthTokensClient`) | Yes | No (`NotSupportedException`) |
| `LiveMusicClient` | Yes | No |

## Prerequisites

```bash
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Live
```

- A Gemini API key, or Vertex AI credentials. See [Authentication](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication).
- A Live model, for example `GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Live` (Gemini API) or `VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Live`
  (Vertex AI). Other Live models include `GoogleAIModels.Gemini38LiveExtendedThinking` and
  `GoogleAIModels.Gemini31FlashLivePreview`.

## Response modality: use AUDIO

Current Live models answer with **audio**. Set `ResponseModalities` to `Modality.AUDIO`. If you pass no
`GenerationConfig`, the client defaults to `Modality.TEXT`, which Live audio models reject. To also get the
answer as text, turn on output transcription.

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Live;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var config = new GenerationConfig
{
    ResponseModalities = new List<Modality> { Modality.AUDIO }
};

using var client = new MultiModalLiveClient(
    new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey),
    GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Live,
    config,
    systemInstruction: "You are a helpful assistant.")
{
    OutputAudioTranscriptionEnabled = true,   // text transcript of the model's audio
    InputAudioTranscriptionEnabled = true     // text transcript of your audio
};
```

You can also create a client from an existing model with the extension method
`generativeModel.CreateMultiModalLiveClient(...)` (namespace `GenerativeAI.Live.Extensions`).

## Events

```csharp
client.Connected += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine("Connected");
client.Disconnected += (_, e) =>
{
    // When the server closes the session with a reason, e is GenerativeAI.Live.Events.ErrorMessageEventArgs.
    if (e is GenerativeAI.Live.Events.ErrorMessageEventArgs closed)
        Console.WriteLine($"Closed by server: {closed.ErrorMessage}");
};
client.ErrorOccurred += (_, e) => Console.WriteLine($"Error: {e.GetException().Message}");

client.AudioChunkReceived += (_, e) => Play(e.Buffer, e.HeaderInfo.SampleRate);   // raw PCM chunk
client.AudioReceiveCompleted += (_, e) => Console.WriteLine($"Turn audio: {e.Buffer.Length} bytes");
client.TextChunkReceived += (_, e) => Console.Write(e.Text);                       // e.IsTurnFinish at the end
client.OutputTranscriptionReceived += (_, t) => Console.Write(t.Text);
client.InputTranscriptionReceived += (_, t) => Console.WriteLine($"You said: {t.Text}");
client.TurnCompleted += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine("\n[turn complete]");
client.GenerationInterrupted += (_, _) => StopPlayback();                           // the user barged in
client.MessageReceived += (_, e) => { /* raw LiveServerMessage in e.Payload */ };
client.GoAwayReceived += (_, goAway) => Console.WriteLine($"Server closing soon, time left: {goAway.TimeLeft}");
client.SessionResumableUpdateReceived += (_, update) => { /* update.NewHandle, update.Resumable */ };
```

`Play` and `StopPlayback` stand for your own audio code. `AudioHelper.AddWaveHeader(...)` can wrap PCM data in a WAV
header.

## Connect and send input

`ConnectAsync` opens the WebSocket and, by default, sends the setup message built from the client's properties.

```csharp
await client.ConnectAsync();

// A complete user turn (client content).
await client.SentTextAsync("Hi! What's the weather like on Mars?");

// Realtime text: processed like streamed audio, and can interrupt the model.
await client.SendRealtimeTextAsync("Actually, tell me about Venus instead.");

// Realtime audio: 16-bit PCM, 16 kHz mono by default ("audio/pcm;rate=16000").
await client.SendAudioAsync(pcmChunk);
await client.SendAudioStreamEndAsync();   // microphone turned off (Gemini API only)

// Video frames (camera or screen capture), JPEG by default.
await client.SendVideoFrameAsync(jpegBytes);

await client.DisconnectAsync();
```

For full control, use `SendClientContentAsync(LiveClientContent)`,
`SendRealtimeInputAsync(LiveClientRealtimeInput)`, `SendToolResponseAsync(...)` and
`SendSetupAsync(LiveClientSetup)` (call `ConnectAsync(autoSendSetup: false)` first).

## Function calling and built-in tools

Set `FunctionTools` (or call `AddFunctionTools(functionTools, toolConfig)`) before connecting. The client calls
your functions when the model requests them and sends the results back. Set `UseGoogleSearch` or `UseCodeExecutor`
to add those tools. See [Function Calling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Function-Calling).

## Transcription

- `InputAudioTranscriptionEnabled` / `OutputAudioTranscriptionEnabled` turn transcription on.
- `InputAudioTranscriptionConfig` / `OutputAudioTranscriptionConfig` (`AudioTranscriptionConfig`) set options such
  as `LanguageCodes`. Setting a config enables transcription even if the matching `...Enabled` flag is false.
- Transcripts arrive through `InputTranscriptionReceived` / `OutputTranscriptionReceived` as `Transcription`
  objects (`Text`, `Finished`, `LanguageCode`, `SpeakerLabel`).

## Manual activity detection

By default the server detects when the user starts and stops speaking. To signal turns yourself, disable automatic
activity detection and wrap each spoken turn in activity markers:

```csharp
client.RealtimeInputConfig = new RealtimeInputConfig
{
    AutomaticActivityDetection = new AutomaticActivityDetection { Disabled = true }
};
await client.ConnectAsync();

await client.SendActivityStartAsync();
await client.SendAudioAsync(pcmChunk);      // one or more audio chunks
await client.SendActivityEndAsync();
```

**Activity markers delimit audio.** The server rejects realtime *text* sent between `SendActivityStartAsync` and
`SendActivityEndAsync` with "Precondition check failed". Send realtime text with `SendRealtimeTextAsync` outside
the markers.

`RealtimeInputConfig` also has `ActivityHandling` and `TurnCoverage`, and `AutomaticActivityDetection` has
`StartOfSpeechSensitivity` and `EndOfSpeechSensitivity` for tuning automatic detection.

## Session resumption

Set `SessionResumption` to receive resumption handles. The client stores the latest resumable handle in
`LastSessionResumptionHandle`. To resume later, pass it as `SessionResumptionConfig.Handle`:

```csharp
client.SessionResumption = new SessionResumptionConfig();
await client.ConnectAsync();
// ... later, before the session ends:
string? handle = client.LastSessionResumptionHandle;

// New client, same conversation:
using var resumed = new MultiModalLiveClient(new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey), GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Live, config)
{
    SessionResumption = new SessionResumptionConfig { Handle = handle }
};
await resumed.ConnectAsync();
```

The server sends handles at its own pace, so `LastSessionResumptionHandle` can stay `null` for a while. When the
WebSocket reconnects, the client re-sends the setup message automatically (`ResendSetupOnReconnect`, default
`true`), using the latest handle if one was received.

## GoAway

The server sends a GoAway message shortly before it ends a connection. Handle `GoAwayReceived`
(`LiveServerGoAway.TimeLeft`) to finish the turn, save `LastSessionResumptionHandle` and reconnect.

## Context window compression

Long sessions can exceed the context window. Enable a sliding window so the server compresses older turns:

```csharp
client.ContextWindowCompression = new ContextWindowCompressionConfig
{
    TriggerTokens = 100_000,
    SlidingWindow = new SlidingWindow { TargetTokens = 50_000 }
};
```

## Update context mid-session

`SendContextUpdateAsync` changes the system instruction and/or tools of a running session without reconnecting:

```csharp
await client.SendContextUpdateAsync("You are a pirate. Answer in one word.");
// Pass tools as the second argument; an empty collection removes all tools, null keeps the current ones.
```

Changing tools this way does not change `FunctionTools`, which the client uses to execute function calls; update it
too if you add or remove function declarations.

## Ephemeral tokens

Client-side apps (browsers, mobile apps) should not hold your API key. Create a short-lived token on your server
with `AuthTokensClient` (Gemini API only), then connect with the token in place of the API key:

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Clients;

// Server side
var tokens = new AuthTokensClient(new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey));
AuthToken token = await tokens.CreateAsync(new CreateAuthTokenConfig
{
    Uses = 1,
    ExpireTime = DateTime.UtcNow.AddMinutes(10),
    NewSessionExpireTime = DateTime.UtcNow.AddMinutes(2),
    LiveConnectConstraints = new LiveClientSetup
    {
        Model = GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Live,
        GenerationConfig = config
    }
});

// Client side: token.Name ("auth_tokens/...") replaces the API key.
using var live = new MultiModalLiveClient(new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(token.Name), GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Live, config);
await live.ConnectAsync();
```

Tokens expire on their own; there is no delete API. `LockAdditionalFields` can lock more setup fields.

## Live Music (Lyria RealTime)

`LiveMusicClient` streams generated music over the Gemini API Live Music endpoint (experimental, Gemini API only).
Audio arrives as raw 16-bit PCM, 48 kHz stereo by default. You can change prompts and config while it plays.

```csharp
using var music = new LiveMusicClient(new GoogleAIPlatformAdapter(apiKey), GoogleAIModels.Music.LyriaRealtimeExp);

music.AudioChunkReceived += (_, e) => Play(e.Data, e.SampleRate, e.Channels);
music.FilteredPromptReceived += (_, e) => Console.WriteLine($"Prompt filtered: {e.Text} ({e.FilteredReason})");
music.ErrorOccurred += (_, e) => Console.WriteLine(e.GetException().Message);

await music.ConnectAsync();   // waits for setupComplete (TimeoutException after SetupTimeout, default 30 s)
await music.SetWeightedPromptsAsync(new[] { new WeightedPrompt { Text = "calm piano", Weight = 1.0 } });
await music.SetMusicGenerationConfigAsync(new LiveMusicGenerationConfig { Bpm = 90 });
await music.PlayAsync();

// Steer while playing, then stop.
await music.SetWeightedPromptsAsync("upbeat jazz");
await music.PauseAsync();
await music.StopAsync();
await music.DisconnectAsync();
```

`ResetContextAsync` resets the music context. There is also a `LiveMusicClient(string? apiKey, ...)` constructor.

## Error handling

- Sending before `ConnectAsync`, or after the socket closed, throws `InvalidOperationException`
  ("The WebSocket client is not connected.") and raises `ErrorOccurred`.
- Server-side rejections (an invalid setup, an unsupported modality, text between activity markers) close the
  session: handle `Disconnected` and check for `ErrorMessageEventArgs`.
- `AuthTokensClient.CreateAsync` throws `GenerativeAI.Exceptions.ApiException` for API errors and
  `NotSupportedException` on Vertex AI.
- `SendSetupAsync` throws `ArgumentException` if the model name has no `models/` (or other `/`) prefix; the
  constructor adds it for you.

## Related pages

- [Authentication](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication)
- [Function Calling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Function-Calling)
- [Multimodal Features](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Multimodal-Features)
- [Agent APIs](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Agent-APIs): custom voices

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/File-Search -->

# File Search

File Search is managed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on the Gemini API. You create a **File Search store**,
add documents to it, and Google chunks, embeds and indexes them. You then give the store to the `FileSearch` tool,
and the model grounds its answers on your documents.

The SDK exposes it through `FileSearchStoresClient` (namespace `GenerativeAI.Clients`).

| Platform | Support |
|---|---|
| Gemini API | Yes |
| Vertex AI | No. Every `FileSearchStoresClient` method and `GenerativeModel.UseFileSearch` throw `NotSupportedException` on Vertex AI. Use the [Vertex RAG Engine](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Vertex-RAG-Engine) there. |

## Prerequisites

- NuGet package: `Google_GenerativeAI`
- A Gemini API key. See [Authentication](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication).

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Clients;
using GenerativeAI.Types;

var googleAi = new GoogleAi(apiKey);
FileSearchStoresClient stores = googleAi.CreateFileSearchStoresClient();
```

## Typical flow

1. Create a store with `CreateFileSearchStoreAsync`.
2. Add files with `UploadToFileSearchStoreAsync` / `UploadStreamToFileSearchStoreAsync`, or import a file that is
   already uploaded through the Files API with `ImportFileAsync`.
3. Wait for indexing with `WaitForOperationAsync`.
4. Pass the store name to the `FileSearch` tool, for example with `GenerativeModel.UseFileSearch`.

## Create, get, list and delete stores

```csharp
// Display name and embedding model are optional.
FileSearchStore store = await stores.CreateFileSearchStoreAsync("product-docs");
Console.WriteLine(store.Name); // "fileSearchStores/..."

var same = await stores.GetFileSearchStoreAsync(store.Name!);
Console.WriteLine($"{same.ActiveDocumentsCount} active, {same.PendingDocumentsCount} pending");

// One page at a time...
var page = await stores.ListFileSearchStoresAsync(pageSize: 20);
// ...or every store.
await foreach (var s in stores.ListAllFileSearchStoresAsync())
    Console.WriteLine($"{s.Name}: {s.DisplayName}");

// force: true also deletes the documents in the store.
await stores.DeleteFileSearchStoreAsync(store.Name!, force: true);
```

Store names can be given as `fileSearchStores/{id}` or just `{id}`.

## Upload files into a store

Upload a local file directly. The MIME type is inferred from the extension if you don't set it:

```csharp
var operation = await stores.UploadToFileSearchStoreAsync(store.Name!, "docs/manual.pdf",
    new UploadToFileSearchStoreConfig
    {
        DisplayName = "manual.pdf",
        CustomMetadata = new List<CustomMetadata> { new("product") { StringValue = "router-x" } },
        ChunkingConfig = new ChunkingConfig
        {
            WhiteSpaceConfig = new WhiteSpaceConfig { MaxTokensPerChunk = 400, MaxOverlapTokens = 40 }
        }
    },
    progressCallback: p => Console.WriteLine($"{p:F0}%"));

operation = await stores.WaitForOperationAsync(operation, timeout: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5));
Console.WriteLine(operation.Response?.DocumentName);
```

Or upload from a stream (the stream is disposed once the upload finishes):

```csharp
using var stream = new MemoryStream(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("Project Bluebird started in 2019."));
var op = await stores.UploadStreamToFileSearchStoreAsync(store.Name!, stream, "text/plain",
    new UploadToFileSearchStoreConfig { DisplayName = "bluebird.txt" });
op = await stores.WaitForOperationAsync(op);
```

## Import a file from the Files API

If you already uploaded the file with the Files API (see [Files Client](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Files-Client)), import it by name:

```csharp
var importOp = await stores.ImportFileAsync(store.Name!, "files/abc123",
    new ImportFileConfig
    {
        CustomMetadata = new List<CustomMetadata> { new("year") { NumericValue = 2024 } }
    });
importOp = await stores.WaitForOperationAsync(importOp);
```

`WaitForOperationAsync` polls every 2 seconds by default and throws `TimeoutException` after 10 minutes unless you
pass other values. You can also poll yourself with `GetOperationAsync(operationName)`. Check
`FileSearchOperation.Error` when `Done` is `true`.

## Manage documents

```csharp
await foreach (var doc in stores.ListAllDocumentsAsync(store.Name!))
    Console.WriteLine($"{doc.Name} {doc.DisplayName} {doc.State}");

var document = await stores.GetDocumentAsync("fileSearchStores/my-store/documents/my-doc");

// force: true also deletes the document's chunks.
await stores.DeleteDocumentAsync(document.Name!, force: true);
```

`DownloadMediaAsync(mediaId)` downloads media referenced by File Search grounding metadata
(`fileSearchStores/{store}/media/{blob}`).

## Use File Search in generation

### With GenerativeModel

`UseFileSearch` adds a `FileSearch` tool to every request of the model:

```csharp
var model = googleAi.CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
model.UseFileSearch(store.Name!);

var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync("What year did Project Bluebird start?");
Console.WriteLine(response.Text());
```

The other overload takes `topK` and an AIP-160 `metadataFilter` over the documents' custom metadata:

```csharp
model.UseFileSearch(new[] { store.Name! }, topK: 5, metadataFilter: "product = \"router-x\"");
```

You can also build the tool yourself (`Tool.FileSearch` with a `FileSearch` object that has
`FileSearchStoreNames`, `TopK` and `MetadataFilter`).

### With the Interactions API

```csharp
var interactions = googleAi.CreateInteractionsClient();
var result = await interactions.CreateAsync(new CreateInteractionRequest
{
    Model = InteractionModels.Gemini38Flash,
    Input = "What year did Project Bluebird start?",
    Tools = new List<InteractionTool>
    {
        new InteractionFileSearchTool { FileSearchStoreNames = new List<string> { store.Name! } }
    }
});
Console.WriteLine(result.OutputText);
```

See [Interactions API](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Interactions-API).

## Error handling

- API errors are thrown as `GenerativeAI.Exceptions.ApiException` (`ErrorCode`, `ErrorStatus`, `ErrorMessage`).
  402/429 means the project has no quota or billing for File Search right now.
- `NotSupportedException` is thrown when the client or model uses Vertex AI.
- `TimeoutException` is thrown by `WaitForOperationAsync` when indexing takes longer than the timeout.

```csharp
try
{
    var store = await stores.CreateFileSearchStoreAsync("docs");
}
catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.ErrorCode is 402 or 429)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"File Search is not available right now: {ex.ErrorMessage}");
}
```

## Related pages

- [Files Client](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Files-Client)
- [Vertex RAG Engine](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Vertex-RAG-Engine): the Vertex AI alternative
- [Interactions API](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Interactions-API)
- [Generate Content](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Generate-Content)
