<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Microsoft.Extensions.AI-IChatClient-Implementation -->

# Microsoft.Extensions.AI Integration (IChatClient)

The **Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft** package implements the [Microsoft.Extensions.AI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/microsoft-extensions-ai) (MEAI) abstractions on top of the SDK, so Gemini can be used anywhere an `IChatClient`, `IEmbeddingGenerator` or `IImageGenerator` is expected, including MEAI middleware (function invocation, logging, caching, telemetry) and dependency injection.

| MEAI abstraction | Implementation | Wraps |
|---|---|---|
| `IChatClient` | `GenerativeAIChatClient` | `GenerativeModel` |
| `IEmbeddingGenerator<string, Embedding<float>>` | `GenerativeAIEmbeddingGenerator` | `EmbeddingModel` (see [Embeddings](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Embeddings)) |
| `IImageGenerator` | `GenerativeAIImageGenerator` (Gemini image models), `GenerativeAIImagenGenerator` (obsolete: Imagen is retired) | see [Image Generation](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Image-Generation) |

## Installation

```bash
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft
```

The package references **Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Abstractions 10.x on net8.0 and net9.0**, and **11.x on net10.0, net11.0, netstandard2.0 and net462**. Middleware such as `UseFunctionInvocation()` and the `AddChatClient(...)` DI helper come from the separate `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` package; add it if you use them, with the same major version.

## Creating the client

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Microsoft;
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;

// Gemini API with an API key (model defaults to GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel)
IChatClient client = new GenerativeAIChatClient(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);

// Any platform adapter, e.g. Vertex AI
IChatClient vertexClient = new GenerativeAIChatClient(
    new VertextPlatformAdapter(projectId: "my-project", region: "us-central1"),
    VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Flash);
```

Constructors:

- `GenerativeAIChatClient(string apiKey, string modelName = GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel, bool autoCallFunction = true)`
- `GenerativeAIChatClient(IPlatformAdapter adapter, string modelName = GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel, bool autoCallFunction = true)`

The underlying `GenerativeModel` is available through the `model` property.

## Basic usage

```csharp
ChatResponse response = await client.GetResponseAsync("What is the capital of France?");
Console.WriteLine(response.Text);
```

### Conversation history

`IChatClient` is stateless: pass the whole conversation each time and append the replies.

```csharp
var history = new List<ChatMessage>
{
    new(ChatRole.System, "You are a helpful assistant."),
    new(ChatRole.User, "Give me three names for a cat.")
};

ChatResponse reply = await client.GetResponseAsync(history);
history.AddMessages(reply);

history.Add(new ChatMessage(ChatRole.User, "Which one is the shortest?"));
reply = await client.GetResponseAsync(history);
Console.WriteLine(reply.Text);
```

System messages, together with `ChatOptions.Instructions`, become the Gemini system instruction.

### Streaming

```csharp
await foreach (ChatResponseUpdate update in client.GetStreamingResponseAsync("Write a haiku about the sea."))
{
    Console.Write(update.Text);
}
```

### Chat options

```csharp
var options = new ChatOptions
{
    Temperature = 0.7f,
    MaxOutputTokens = 1024,
    TopP = 0.9f,
    TopK = 40,
    StopSequences = new List<string> { "END" },
    Seed = 42,
    ResponseFormat = ChatResponseFormat.Json // or ChatResponseFormat.ForJsonSchema(...)
};

ChatResponse response = await client.GetResponseAsync(history, options);
```

`Temperature`, `TopP`, `TopK`, `MaxOutputTokens`, `StopSequences`, `Seed`, `PresencePenalty`, `FrequencyPenalty` and `ResponseFormat` map to Gemini's `GenerationConfig`. A JSON schema in `ResponseFormat` is converted to the schema subset Gemini accepts. Structured output helpers such as `client.GetResponseAsync<T>(...)` from `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` work as well.

### Gemini-specific options

Use `ChatOptions.AdditionalProperties` with the keys in `AdditionalPropertiesKeys`:

| Key | Value type | Gemini setting |
|---|---|---|
| `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ThinkingBudget` | `int?` | `ThinkingConfig.ThinkingBudget` |
| `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ThinkingConfigIncludeThoughts` | `bool?` | `ThinkingConfig.IncludeThoughts` |
| `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ResponseModalities` | `List<Modality>` | `ResponseModalities` (for example text + image) |
| `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ImageConfigAspectRatio` | `string` | `ImageConfig.AspectRatio` |
| `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ImageConfigImageSize` | `string` | `ImageConfig.ImageSize` |
| `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ImageOutputOptionsMimeType` | `string` | `ImageConfig.ImageOutputOptions.MimeType` |
| `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ImageOutputOptionsCompressionQuality` | `int` | `ImageConfig.ImageOutputOptions.CompressionQuality` |
| `"ResponseLogprobs"` / `"Logprobs"` | `bool?` / `int?` | log probabilities |

```csharp
var options = new ChatOptions
{
    AdditionalProperties = new AdditionalPropertiesDictionary
    {
        [AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ThinkingBudget] = 1024,
        [AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ThinkingConfigIncludeThoughts] = true
    }
};
```

Thought signatures returned by Gemini 3.x are kept in the `AdditionalProperties` of the returned contents (key `AdditionalPropertiesKeys.ThoughtSignature`) and sent back when you pass the messages in the next request, which multi-turn function calling with thinking models needs.

### Multimodal input

Add `DataContent` (bytes plus media type) to a message; it is sent as inline data. `DataContent` larger than 20 MB is uploaded through the Files API automatically instead. To reference a file you already uploaded (see [Files Client](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Files-Client)), use the SDK's `RemoteFileContent(RemoteFile remoteFile, string? mimeType = null)` from `GenerativeAI.Microsoft.Extensions`. Other content types such as `UriContent` are not converted and are skipped.

```csharp
var message = new ChatMessage(ChatRole.User, new List<AIContent>
{
    new TextContent("Describe this picture."),
    new DataContent(await File.ReadAllBytesAsync("photo.jpg"), "image/jpeg")
});

ChatResponse response = await client.GetResponseAsync(message);
```

## Function calling

### Built-in function calling (default)

With `autoCallFunction: true` (the default) the client runs the `AIFunction`s in `ChatOptions.Tools` itself and sends the results back to the model:

```csharp
var options = new ChatOptions
{
    Tools = new List<AITool> { AIFunctionFactory.Create(GetWeather) }
};

ChatResponse response = await client.GetResponseAsync("What's the weather in Paris?", options);
Console.WriteLine(response.Text);

[Description("Gets the current weather for a city")]
static string GetWeather(string city) => $"It's sunny in {city}.";
```

### Hosted tools

`HostedWebSearchTool` in `ChatOptions.Tools` turns on Gemini's Google Search tool, and `HostedCodeInterpreterTool` turns on code execution.

### Using MEAI's FunctionInvokingChatClient

To use MEAI's function-invocation middleware instead, turn the built-in loop off with `autoCallFunction: false`:

```csharp
IChatClient client = new GenerativeAIChatClient(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash, autoCallFunction: false)
    .AsBuilder()
    .UseFunctionInvocation()
    .Build();
```

You can also change it later with the `AutoCallFunction` property.

### Tools from the SDK's tool generators

The source-generated and reflection-based tools from `Google_GenerativeAI.Tools` (see [Function Calling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Function-Calling)) convert to MEAI tools:

```csharp
// Method-based: [FunctionTool(MeaiFunctionTool = true)]
options.Tools = new Tools([GetCurrentDateTime]).AsMeaiTools();

// Interface-based: [GenerateJsonSchema(MeaiFunctionTool = true)]
options.Tools = new WeatherService().AsMeaiTools();

// Reflection-based
options.Tools = new List<AITool> { new QuickTool(GetCurrentDateTime).AsMeaiTool() };
```

### v4.0.0 fixes

- **Parallel function calls:** when the model asks for several functions in one turn, the model's function-call turn is added to the history once, followed by all function results in one turn. Earlier versions repeated the function-call turn for every call.
- **Streaming function-call detection:** `GetStreamingResponseAsync` collects parts across the whole stream, so function calls are found even when the last chunk only carries the finish reason (common with newer models).
- **`user` role for function results:** results are sent with the `user` role because Gemini 3.x rejects the `function` role.

## Dependency injection

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Microsoft;
using Microsoft.Extensions.AI;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

string apiKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GOOGLE_API_KEY")!;

// Plain registration (Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft only)
services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>(_ => new GenerativeAIChatClient(apiKey));

// Or with the MEAI builder and middleware (needs the Microsoft.Extensions.AI package)
services.AddChatClient(_ => new GenerativeAIChatClient(apiKey, GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash, autoCallFunction: false))
        .UseFunctionInvocation();
```

Inject `IChatClient` into your services:

```csharp
public class MyChatService(IChatClient chatClient)
{
    public async Task<string> AskAsync(string userMessage)
    {
        ChatResponse response = await chatClient.GetResponseAsync(userMessage);
        return response.Text;
    }
}
```

For the SDK's own DI integration (`IGenerativeAiService`), see [Web Application Integration](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Web-Application-Integration).

## Important considerations

1. **API keys:** keep keys out of source code; use environment variables, user secrets or a secret store.
2. **Errors:** handle exceptions from API calls (for example `GenerativeAIException` and HTTP errors).
3. **Rate limits:** respect the API's rate limits and add retries or throttling where needed.
4. **Context window:** long conversations can exceed the model's context window; trim or summarize older messages.
5. **Model choice:** pick the model for your task and budget; see [Supported Models](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Supported-Models).

## References

- [Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI.Microsoft)
- [Microsoft.Extensions.AI documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/microsoft-extensions-ai)
- [Function Calling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Function-Calling) · [Image Generation](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Image-Generation) · [Embeddings](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Embeddings) · [MCP Integration](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/MCP-(Model-Context-Protocol)-Integration)

<!-- Source: https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Web-Application-Integration -->

# Web Application Integration

The [**Google_GenerativeAI.Web**](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Google_GenerativeAI.Web/) package registers the SDK with the .NET dependency injection container. It adds `IServiceCollection` extension methods that bind `GenerativeAIOptions`, set up authentication, and register `IGenerativeAiService`, which you inject into controllers, minimal API handlers or other services.

The package targets net6.0 to net10.0 (plus net11.0) and netstandard2.0. It depends on `Google_GenerativeAI` and `Google_GenerativeAI.Auth`.

## Installation

```bash
dotnet add package Google_GenerativeAI.Web
```

## Registering the services

All overloads live in `GenerativeAI.Web.ServiceCollectionExtension` and register `IGenerativeAiService` as a transient service.

### 1. From environment variables

```csharp
using GenerativeAI.Web;

builder.Services.AddGenerativeAI();
```

With no explicit options, values come from environment variables:

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `Credentials.ApiKey` | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | empty |
| `ProjectId` | `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` | none |
| `Region` | `GOOGLE_REGION` | `us-central1` |
| `Model` | `GOOGLE_AI_MODEL` | `GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel` |
| `IsVertex` | none | `true` if `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` is set, otherwise `false` |
| `ExpressMode` | none | `false` |

### 2. With a `GenerativeAIOptions` object

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Web;

builder.Services.AddGenerativeAI(new GenerativeAIOptions
{
    Model = GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash,
    Credentials = new GoogleAICredentials
    {
        ApiKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GOOGLE_API_KEY")
                 ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("GOOGLE_API_KEY is not set")
    }
});
```

For Vertex AI, set `IsVertex = true` with `ProjectId` and `Region` and configure authentication (see below):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddGenerativeAI(new GenerativeAIOptions
{
    IsVertex = true,
    ProjectId = "your-project-id",
    Region = "us-central1",
    Model = VertexAIModels.Gemini.Gemini38Flash
}).WithAdc();
```

**v4 behaviour: `IsVertex` inference.** When you pass a `GenerativeAIOptions` object without setting `IsVertex`, and it has an API key but no `ProjectId` (and `ExpressMode` is not `true`), `IsVertex` is set to `false`. The service then uses the Gemini API even if `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` happens to be set in the environment. Otherwise an unset `IsVertex` falls back to the environment-based default above. Set `IsVertex` explicitly if you need a specific platform.

### 3. From an `IConfiguration` section

```csharp
builder.Services.AddGenerativeAI(builder.Configuration.GetSection("GenerativeAI"));
```

Or by section path (binds with `BindConfiguration` and validates on start):

```csharp
builder.Services.AddGenerativeAI("GenerativeAI");
```

**appsettings.json**

```json
{
  "GenerativeAI": {
    "Model": "models/gemini-3.8-flash",
    "Credentials": {
      "ApiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
    }
  }
}
```

Vertex AI:

```json
{
  "GenerativeAI": {
    "IsVertex": true,
    "ProjectId": "your-project-id",
    "Region": "us-central1",
    "Model": "gemini-3.8-flash",
    "ExpressMode": false
  }
}
```

With a configuration section, an unset `IsVertex` uses the environment-based default (`true` only when `GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID` is set).

### 4. With an action

```csharp
builder.Services.AddGenerativeAI(options =>
{
    options.Model = GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash;
    options.Credentials = new GoogleAICredentials(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GOOGLE_API_KEY")!);
});
```

`services.ConfigureGenerativeAI(options => { ... })` adjusts the options after registration.

### `GenerativeAIOptions`

```csharp
public class GenerativeAIOptions : IGenerativeAIOptions
{
    public string? ProjectId { get; set; }
    public string? Region { get; set; }
    public IGoogleAuthenticator? Authenticator { get; set; }
    public GoogleAICredentials? Credentials { get; set; }
    public bool? IsVertex { get; set; }
    public string? Model { get; set; }
    public bool? ExpressMode { get; set; }
    public string? ApiVersion { get; set; }
}
```

The Gemini API path requires `Credentials.ApiKey`; without it the service throws `InvalidOperationException("API Key is required for Google AI configuration.")` when it is created.

## Authentication

Extension methods set `GenerativeAIOptions.Authenticator` (authenticators come from `Google_GenerativeAI.Auth`):

| Method | Authenticator |
|---|---|
| `WithAdc()` | `GoogleCloudAdcAuthenticator` (Application Default Credentials) |
| `WithServiceAccount(string jsonFilePath)` | `GoogleServiceAccountAuthenticator` from a JSON key file |
| `WithServiceAccount(string serviceAccountEmail, string certificateFilePath, string passPhrase)` | `GoogleServiceAccountAuthenticator` from a certificate |
| `WithOAuth(string clientSecretFilePath)` | `GoogleOAuthAuthenticator` |

They return `void`, so call them last:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddGenerativeAI(options)
                .WithServiceAccount("path/to/service_account.json");
```

See [Authentication](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Authentication) for details.

## Using `IGenerativeAiService`

```csharp
public interface IGenerativeAiService
{
    IGenerativeAI Platform { get; }
    IGenerativeModel CreateInstance(string modelName = GoogleAIModels.DefaultGeminiModel);
}
```

`CreateInstance` uses its `modelName` argument, not `GenerativeAIOptions.Model`, so pass the model you want.

### Controller

```csharp
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Web;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("gemini")]
public class GeminiController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IGenerativeAiService _generativeAiService;

    public GeminiController(IGenerativeAiService generativeAiService) =>
        _generativeAiService = generativeAiService;

    [HttpGet("generate")]
    public async Task<string> GenerateAsync(string prompt)
    {
        var model = _generativeAiService.CreateInstance(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
        var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(prompt);
        return response.Text;
    }
}
```

### Minimal API

```csharp
app.MapGet("/generate", async (string prompt, IGenerativeAiService ai) =>
{
    var model = ai.CreateInstance(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
    var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(prompt);
    return response.Text;
});
```

`IGenerativeModel` also provides `StreamContentAsync(...)` for streaming responses (see [Streaming](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Streaming)). Use `Platform` to reach the underlying `GoogleAi` or `VertexAI` instance.

A complete sample is in [`samples/WebAppIntegration`](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/tree/main/samples/WebAppIntegration).

## Microsoft.Extensions.AI in web apps

If your app uses `IChatClient`, register `GenerativeAIChatClient` directly; see [Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Microsoft.Extensions.AI-IChatClient-Implementation#dependency-injection).

## Important considerations

1. Make sure the environment variables or configuration values are set.
2. Choose an authentication method that fits your hosting environment (API key, ADC, service account or OAuth).
3. Keep API keys and service-account files out of source control.

- [GenerativeAI.Web](https://gunpal5.github.io/generative-ai/search.html?SearchText=GenerativeAI.Web)

# NativeAOT and Trimming Guidelines

NativeAOT and trimming make applications smaller and faster to start, but they restrict runtime reflection and dynamic code generation. This page explains which parts of the SDK work without changes and where you need to supply your own `JsonSerializerContext`.

## What works without changes

- **SDK request and response types.** All built-in types are serialized with System.Text.Json source generation, so no reflection-based serialization is needed for the SDK's own types:
  - `TypesSerializerContext` (namespace `GenerativeAI.Types`): the core context used by `DefaultSerializerOptions.Options` for content generation, chat, embeddings, files, caching, models, batch, Live API setup, auth tokens and more.
  - Separate contexts for newer API areas. Each client puts its context first in its own resolver chain:

    | Context | Used by |
    |---|---|
    | `FileSearchSerializerContext` | `FileSearchStoresClient` (File Search stores and documents) |
    | `InteractionsSerializerContext` | `InteractionsClient` (Interactions API) and, for shared types, the agent API clients |
    | `WebhooksSerializerContext` | `WebhooksClient` |
    | `TuningSerializerContext` | `TuningClient` |
    | `AgentApisSerializerContext` | `AgentsClient`, `VoicesClient`, `EnvironmentsClient`, `TriggersClient`, `CredentialsClient`, `DecisionsClient` |

    These are separate contexts rather than partials of `TypesSerializerContext` because the System.Text.Json source generator shipped for net6.0 to net10.0 and netstandard2.0 fails when `[JsonSerializable]` attributes are split across partial declarations.
- **Source-generated function tools.** Tools defined with `[FunctionTool]` or `[GenerateJsonSchema]` (see [Function Calling](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Function-Calling)) generate their schemas and call code at compile time.

The repository's `tests/AotTest` project (`<PublishAot>true</PublishAot>`) exercises these paths.

## What needs your own `JsonSerializerContext`

Your own types are not known to the SDK's contexts. You must register them when you use:

- **JSON mode** (`GenerateObjectAsync<T>`, `UseJsonMode<T>`, `ToObject<T>`), see [JSON Mode](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Json-Mode)
- **Reflection-based `QuickTool` / `QuickTools`**, for parameter and return types

### JSON mode

```csharp
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;
using GenerativeAI;

public class MyData
{
    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public int Age { get; set; }
}

[JsonSerializable(typeof(MyData))]
public partial class MyDataJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext { }
```

Then register it in one of three ways (see [Passing a JsonSerializerContext](#passing-a-jsonserializercontext)):

```csharp
// Option 1: global
DefaultSerializerOptions.CustomJsonTypeResolvers.Add(MyDataJsonContext.Default);

// Option 2: per GenerativeModel instance
generativeModel.GenerateObjectJsonSerializerOptions = MyDataJsonContext.Default.Options;

// Option 3: per request / response
var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
request.UseJsonMode<MyData>(MyDataJsonContext.Default.Options);
```

### QuickTools (reflection-based)

Register every parameter type and return type used by the tool:

```csharp
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;
using GenerativeAI;
using GenerativeAI.Tools;

public class ToolInput  { public string InputText { get; set; } = string.Empty; }
public class ToolOutput { public int Result { get; set; } }

[JsonSerializable(typeof(ToolInput))]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(ToolOutput))]
public partial class MyToolJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext { }

public static class MyTools
{
    public static ToolOutput MyToolMethod(ToolInput input) => new() { Result = input.InputText.Length };
}

// Option 1: global
DefaultSerializerOptions.CustomJsonTypeResolvers.Add(MyToolJsonContext.Default);

// Option 2: pass the options to the constructor
var quickTool = new QuickTool(MyTools.MyToolMethod, options: MyToolJsonContext.Default.Options);
```

`QuickTools(Delegate[] delegates, JsonSerializerOptions? options = null)` accepts the same options for several delegates.

## Passing a JsonSerializerContext

1. **Global.** Add the context to `DefaultSerializerOptions.CustomJsonTypeResolvers` at startup. It is then used by JSON mode and QuickTools everywhere in the application.

    ```csharp
    using GenerativeAI;

    public static void ConfigureJsonContext()
    {
        DefaultSerializerOptions.CustomJsonTypeResolvers.Add(MyDataJsonContext.Default);
    }
    ```

2. **`GenerativeModel` scope.** Set `GenerateObjectJsonSerializerOptions` on a model instance. You can skip this if the context is already registered globally.

    ```csharp
    using GenerativeAI;

    public async Task<MyData?> UseModelScopedContext(string apiKey, string prompt)
    {
        var googleAi = new GoogleAi(apiKey);
        var model = googleAi.CreateGenerativeModel(GoogleAIModels.Gemini38Flash);
        model.GenerateObjectJsonSerializerOptions = MyDataJsonContext.Default.Options;

        return await model.GenerateObjectAsync<MyData>(prompt);
    }
    ```

3. **Request / response level.** Pass the options to `GenerateContentRequest.UseJsonMode<T>(options)` and `GenerateContentResponse.ToObject<T>(options)`.

    ```csharp
    using GenerativeAI;
    using GenerativeAI.Types;

    public async Task UseRequestSpecificContext(GenerativeModel model, string prompt)
    {
        var request = new GenerateContentRequest();
        request.AddText(prompt);
        request.UseJsonMode<MyData>(MyDataJsonContext.Default.Options);

        var response = await model.GenerateContentAsync(request);
        var myData = response.ToObject<MyData>(MyDataJsonContext.Default.Options);

        Console.WriteLine($"Name: {myData?.Name}, Age: {myData?.Age}");
    }
    ```

## Microsoft.Extensions.AI

`GenerativeAIChatClient` and the other MEAI adapters (see [Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient](https://github.com/gunpal5/Google_GenerativeAI/wiki/Microsoft.Extensions.AI-IChatClient-Implementation)) use the same serialization. For tools, prefer `[FunctionTool(MeaiFunctionTool = true)]` or `[GenerateJsonSchema(MeaiFunctionTool = true)]` and their generated `AsMeaiTools()`. If you use `new QuickTool(...).AsMeaiTool()`, register your types as shown above.

## Important considerations

- **Register every type.** All types used in JSON mode and QuickTools must be in a `JsonSerializerContext`; a missing type causes a runtime error in AOT or trimmed builds.
- **Performance.** Pre-generated serialization code also improves startup time and throughput.
- **Trimming.** The trimmer removes unused code; a `JsonSerializerContext` keeps the serialization code your types need.
- **Reflection limits.** Prefer source generation and explicit type registration over runtime reflection.
- **Check warnings.** Publish with `dotnet publish -c Release` (with `PublishAot` or `PublishTrimmed`) and fix any `IL2026`/`IL3050` warnings that point at your own reflection-based code.
